rules.banned_because: Someone else's names, kept out of everything Euphonia publishes (Appendix E; setting/ip-review.md).
rules.fey_type_because: "Fey" survives only as the creature type; the setting's prose says "fae" (Book Two, What's Different). The 2024 rules' own names keep it too: Fey Ancestry, Fey Touched, Fey Wanderer, Summon Fey and the SRD's Conjure Fey (Chat, 15 November). So does a list of creature types: "any Undead, Fey, or Elemental".
rules.renames_because: The setting's own names for those planes, the first two of the Revelator's Cosmography: the Feywild is the Hidden, the Shadowfell the Ghostlands (setting/whats-out.md, wheel-and-plenum.md). The SRD's "the Feywild" reads "the Hidden".

intro.title: The Crossroads
intro.text: Two roads cross in the dust, and a stranger sits where they meet, as if waiting for you. *"I keep nothing you tell me. Answer quickly, and I'll show you who is waiting on your road."*

plain.title: A Few Questions
plain.text: Four questions with pictures, five with two answers and a map. Then three people from this book who fit your answers, each ready to play in a first session.

reveal.title: These are waiting on your road.
reveal.plain_title: Three people who fit your answers.
reveal.more: Not them? There are others on the road.
reveal.plain_more: None of these? See three more, or build your own.

dilemmas.title: The ship at Sofala
dilemmas.scene: A trading ship comes into Mutapa's great port with a sick crew under a yellow flag, and asks to dock. The harbor master has left it to you.

options.label: Open the harbor and treat the sick
options.said: you opened the harbor to a sick ship
options.cost: Whatever the crew has, the port may catch

options.label: Keep the harbor closed
options.said: you kept the harbor closed to keep your own people safe
options.cost: The ship sails on with its sick, and you watch it go

dilemmas.scene: On the road outside a village in Safavid Persia, one of the Hidden offers you a gift, freely, for your name.

options.label: Say nothing, and set his instruments right tonight
options.said: you stood by your teacher and fixed his instruments yourself

options.said: you met the collector's men at the mouth of the valley

options.label: Go up to the mountain's shrine and ask for the water

teach.attack: Roll a d20 and add your attack bonus. If the total equals or beats the target's Armor Class, you hit and roll the damage. A 20 on the die always hits and is a Critical Hit: roll the damage dice twice. A 1 always misses.
teach.signature: This is what they do best. Each use spends one of the marks beside it, and the marks come back on the rest it names.
teach.help: Take the Help action to give an ally Advantage: on their next attack roll against an enemy within 5 feet of you, or on their next check with a skill or tool you're proficient in. It lasts until the start of your next turn. With Advantage you roll two d20s and keep the higher.
teach.help_short: Give an ally Advantage on their next attack or check.
teach.try: Roll a d20 and add the bonus beside the ability it takes. The DM sets the number to reach; equal it or beat it and you do it.
teach.short: An hour of quiet. Spend Hit Point Dice to heal: roll each one, add your Constitution modifier and regain that many Hit Points. Uses that come back on a Short Rest return.
teach.long: A night: eight hours, with at least six of sleep. You regain all your Hit Points and Hit Point Dice, and uses that come back on a rest return.

regions: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

roster.name: Abbas-qoli the Teller
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A naqqal who tells the Shahnameh off Isfahan's great square, acting every hero.
roster.scene: A coffeehouse off the Maidan after the evening prayer, every bench full. A grey-bearded man on a stool, a stick in his hand, is Rostam, then Sohrab, then Rostam again, and when the father learns whom he has killed, a room of grown men is weeping into their coffee. He stops there. The room groans. He holds out his cap for coppers and refuses, absolutely, to say what happens tomorrow.
roster.play: You tell the old heroes' stories and fight like one of them, a mask for every turn of the tale.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: The storyteller's gift for making the hard thing look effortless.

roster.name: Abdul Wahid
roster.line: The Surat market inspector's clerk, who reads every foreigner's license and checks whether the man who signed it still holds office.
roster.scene: Behind the customs house at Surat, a clerk's room with one good window. A thin young man in a white cap holds a Company wizard's permit up to the light, reads it twice, and asks the wizard, politely, after the health of the official who signed it. The wizard says he is well. The clerk says, still politely, that he died in the spring. Then he offers everyone tea.
roster.play: You read people and papers alike, and you know who is lying before they finish the sentence.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Forewarned
signature.line: A shouted warning that lets his friends brace for what the enemy is about to do.

roster.name: Abel Fenwick
roster.line: A Cornish dwarf trained at Lanternhall, now ship's surgeon to the Brethren of the Coast at Port Royal.
roster.scene: A Spanish beach at first light, after the landing. A buccaneer is down in the surf with a pike wound and the Spanish line is reforming at the treeline. The dwarf behind the boats draws his longbow, puts an arrow into the back of the man in the surf, and the man gets up swearing. The second arrow goes into the Spanish sergeant, who discovers that his wound won't close. "The light," the dwarf says to nobody, "is terrible."
roster.play: Your bow is your medicine chest: one arrow heals a friend far away, the next is just an arrow.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Arrow of Healing
signature.line: A medicated shot that heals a friend wherever the arrow lands.

roster.name: Agata Mangano
roster.line: A Catanese charlatan under Etna whose power is the mountain coming through.
roster.scene: At the fair under the Benedictines' wall she is reading a farmer's palm for two grani when the cup of wine on her table shivers. Nobody else notices. She stops talking in the middle of his future, puts both hands flat on the lava flagstones, and says, quite quietly, "Not this year. Next spring. North of Nicolosi." Then she remembers who she is supposed to be, and charges him double.
roster.play: Your power builds like the mountain's; you harden into stone where nothing moves you, then let it out and bury your foe.
roster.class_note: Has a raw force coming through them that builds until it's let out.

signature.name: Release
signature.line: Stone and fire let out on one foe, burying it where it stands.

roster.name: Aisulu
roster.line: A Kazakh batyr of giant blood who rides watch for her camp against Dzungar raiders and the Wild Hunt alike.
roster.scene: A ridge of the autumn pasture at dusk, the camp's riders strung out along it. One of them stands in her stirrups a head taller than any rider on the line, a golden eagle on her arm. Something moves in the dusk below that isn't a fox. She looses the eagle, then lowers her lance, and the line goes down the slope behind her.
roster.play: You ride into the fight raging, with the beasts' own strength in you.
roster.class_note: Fights in a fury that is a state of mind, and is hard to put down.

signature.name: Rage
signature.line: She rages: blows glance off her, hers land harder, and the wild comes into her.

roster.name: Aj K'in Kuch
roster.line: An Itza priest at Nojpetén who reads the k'atun count for the Aj Kan Ek' and has seen why it is not yet time.
roster.scene: Temple steps at Nojpetén at dawn, the lake still. An old priest sits with a folded screenfold book across his knees. A Franciscan friar has paddled across the lake to bring the Itza the faith. The priest receives him courteously, opens the book to the right k'atun, and tells him, politely and precisely, that he has come twenty-nine years too early.
roster.play: You weigh whoever stands against you and take the blow meant for the one beside you.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Favors
signature.line: The planes answering: a vista opened on the Bridgehead, and a foe Weighed.

roster.name: Akinwale
roster.line: A front-rank horseman of Oyo, ridden by his orisha in battle, who remembers none of it.
roster.scene: The Nupe line is set on the far bank, spears grounded, and Oyo's horsemen come down to the ford at a walk. Halfway across, one of them stops riding like a man. His back straightens, his face is somebody else's, and the horse, which knows, goes from a walk to a gallop without being asked. The men on the bank remember afterward that he was laughing. He doesn't remember any of it.
roster.play: You charge from the saddle with a lance; when the orisha rides you, you leap and ride like no mortal man.
roster.class_note: Keeps an oath so hard it becomes a power.

signature.name: Peerless Athlete
signature.line: Ridden by his orisha: for an hour he runs, leaps and rides beyond any man.

roster.name: Akosua Nyarko
roster.line: An Akan hunter who walks the forest's edge for her village, keeps the owners' rules and deals with what doesn't.
roster.scene: The harmattan haze over the forest's edge behind Accra, a shrine where the path enters the trees. A wiry woman with a flintlock older than she is crouches over a line of footprints a foot long that point the wrong way, back the way they came, and laughs quietly. Then she tells you to step exactly where she steps, and not to answer if anything in the trees calls your name.
roster.play: You know the forest's rules and keep them; what breaks them meets your iron.
roster.class_note: Knows the ground, and what comes over it.

signature.name: Cold Iron
signature.line: Iron in every arrow: a harder hit, and a Hidden creature can't teleport away.

roster.name: Alasdair Rua MacAskill
roster.line: A Skye farmer who goes in after the people the Hidden carry off, and doesn't let go.
roster.scene: A shieling on the hill above the sea loch, the eve of Samhain. Everyone is singing but the red-haired man by the door, who hasn't touched his cup. When the door blows open and the light goes strange, he is across the floor before the fiddler stops, and the thing that came in for the youngest girl finds a hand on its arm it can't get out of. It turns to smoke. The hand stays where it was.
roster.play: You grab the thing that matters and hold on while your friends do the rest; when a friend is about to be taken, you hold them instead.
roster.class_note: Fights in a fury that is a state of mind, and is hard to put down.

signature.name: Rage
signature.line: He rages and takes hold: what he grips stays gripped, through every shape it puts on.

roster.name: Alfa Mahmud Gurdu
roster.line: Keeper of a Timbuktu family library that has outlasted conquest, and a master of the science of letters.
roster.scene: A family library near the Sankore mosque, in the cool before noon. A very old man in white lies on a mat with a manuscript propped on his chest, eyes shut. A student in the corner reads a line aloud. "Accusative," says the old man, without opening his eyes, and the student reads it again. The door behind you has a line of letters painted over it. You notice, a moment too late, that you can't read them, and that you can't move your foot across them either.
roster.play: Your work is protection: written names on you and your friends that take the blows first.
roster.class_note: The licensed scholar of magic, most likely to hold a post.

signature.name: Arcane Ward
signature.line: A ward of written letters that takes blows before he does, and tops up with every protection he casts.

roster.name: Alvise Trevisan
roster.line: A Venetian boatman who rows the lagoon at night, and walked the river of death in a fever as a boy.
roster.scene: Cannaregio after midnight, in a fog so thick the campanile has gone. A black sandolo slides up to the San Marcuola steps with a lamp on its prow that burns a color the canal doesn't reflect. The boatman holds out his palm before anyone has said where they're going. Behind him in the stern sit two passengers no one saw get in, wet to the skin and very patient. When the Ten's men come running down the fondamenta, the fog closes over the boat, and there is only the sound of an oar.
roster.play: You keep two spirits at once, one to scout the way and one to carry the slowest out of danger.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Favors
signature.line: The far shore answering: spirits called, and a drowning friend held on this side.

roster.name: Amai Rutendo Chigumba
roster.line: Keeper of the king's granary at Sofala, who knows how many mouths a season holds.
roster.scene: Dusk at the granary door in Sofala's new quarter, a line of journeymen with bowls. A broad woman with a ladle serves each one sadza and relish and says his name before he can say it; the ones who arrived this month she asks about their mothers. A guild master in good clothes comes to the end of the line with his own bowl. She serves him exactly what she served the boy in front of him, and he thanks her.
roster.play: You keep a great store in order and the people it feeds alive; when trouble comes, you had already laid something by.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The grain was already moved, the door already barred: a preparation she made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Ambuya Rudo Gumbo
roster.line: The senior royal medium of Mutapa, through whom a dead king speaks on rain and war.
roster.scene: The court on the plateau, the day the royal spirit is to be asked a question. An old woman in black cloth sits on a mat with her staff across her knees, and the king's counsellors sit very still. She answers the first question in her own voice, tartly. Then, without any warning at all, she doesn't: the voice that answers the second question is a man's, two hundred years old, and it has views about the shewstones.
roster.play: You heal and you speak for the dead, and lately the dead king has said things the living one doesn't want to hear.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Preserve Life
signature.line: A breath of the divine that gets the fallen back on their feet.

roster.name: Ammakka
roster.line: A dwarf diamond appraiser of Golconda, testing whether a diamond can do for magic what platinum does for Mutapa.
roster.scene: The grading sheds at Kollur at dawn, the merchants not yet arrived. A dwarf woman of about a hundred and forty holds a rough stone in tongs in a lamp flame, two fingers on her own wrist, timing something by her pulse, and mutters a number in Telugu. The stone does not change. She writes the number down, frowns, and moves the lamp three fingers to the left. Behind her, a scorched patch on the wall marks the last time the stone did change.
roster.play: You carry two experiments a day and choose their energy as you throw; sometimes they bite back.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Experiments
signature.line: Two sealed vessels a day, each released in the energy she chooses as she mixes it.

roster.name: Amritnath
roster.line: A Nath siddha who found the Font of life inside his own body, and burns with it.
roster.scene: Dawn on the pilgrim road above the Ganges plain, the snows white to the north. A man in ash and ochre sits beside a fire he lit last night and hasn't fed since. The great rings in his split ears catch the light. A raja's men have been waiting since moonrise to ask him how to live forever. He doesn't look up. When he finally speaks, the fire leans toward him, and the air over it shakes the way it does over a road in summer, and the oldest of the raja's men realizes he saw this same yogi, looking exactly this age, when he was a boy.
roster.play: You pay for magic with your own vitality: fire for your foes, healing for your friends, from the same source.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Life-Fused Casting
signature.line: A Prowess Die poured into his fire, to burn one foe hotter or heal one friend.

roster.name: Ana Kitumba
roster.line: A captain of Palmares, born free in the quilombo, whose oath is to the people who got free and the ones still coming.
roster.scene: The palisade at Macaco at dusk. A captain of thirty-three walks the wall with a spear and a Portuguese musket, greeting every sentry by name and asking after their families. A boy on the wall asks whether the expedition will come this year. She tells him the truth, and then she tells him what she will do about it, and he believes her, because she has never once failed.
roster.play: You stand between your people and whoever comes for them, and your oath makes your blade blaze.
roster.class_note: Keeps an oath so hard it becomes a power.

signature.name: Sacred Weapon
signature.line: Her blade blazes with holy light and finds its mark more often.

roster.name: Anselme Lafrenaye
roster.line: A halfling gamester who reads every table in Paris and calls the odds before the dice land.
roster.scene: The Grand Divertissement, July 1668, in the king's pleasure house at Versailles. Two in the morning; the fireworks are over and the play isn't. At the end of the lansquenet table there is a chair with a cushion two thick, and in it a gray-templed halfling in last year's good coat, who has just watched a marquis lose a regiment. He doesn't smile. He almost does, the way a man smiles at weather he predicted and can't do anything about, and then he picks up the cards and tells the marquis, very kindly, which of his tenants he'll have to sell.
roster.play: You watch, you call the swing before it's made, and your friends' blows land where you said they would.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: The Count
signature.line: He calls a friend's swing before the dice land; if it hits, it bites deeper.

roster.name: Asiga
roster.line: A Chamorro makåhna of Hagåtña, a healer and speaker to the ancestors, watching the Spanish mission arrive.
roster.scene: The beach at Hagåtña in June, the whole town come down to see the ship. At the edge of the crowd a woman of forty-four with a basket of medicines on her hip studies the black-robed men coming ashore the way she would study a new plant: what it is, where it grows, what it cures, what it kills. Her daughter, beside her, is just curious. That is what worries her.
roster.play: You heal and speak to the ancestors, and the land lends you its strength when your family needs it.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Land's Aid
signature.line: The land's own strength, hurting foes and healing a friend in one breath.

roster.name: Avdotya Shchukina
roster.line: A Cossack widow who runs a sable-smuggling family from a tavern in Tobolsk, and decides which runner knows what.
roster.scene: A tavern below the Tobolsk kremlin, smoke and kvass. A Cossack widow pours a cup for a governor's clerk with one hand, and slides a sable pelt to him under the table with her foot, and asks after his mother. He drinks. The pelt is gone. So is the inspection of her cellar he was going to make tomorrow.
roster.play: You keep your people fed and their mouths shut; when trouble comes, the sledge was already waiting.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The sledge was already waiting, the clerk already paid: a preparation she made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Avetik of Julfa
roster.line: A New Julfa merchant's younger son sent to Astrakhan to learn silk, who learned nard instead and wins from Kalmyk princes.
roster.scene: The Armenian caravanserai in Astrakhan, a nard table, a Kalmyk prince across it with a falcon on his wrist. A young merchant rolls double sixes, apologizes, and rolls them again. The prince looks at the dice. The young man offers him the dice to inspect. They are honest. That is the worst part.
roster.play: You read the table, call the odds and win; your friends' blows land where you said they would.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: The Count
signature.line: He calls a friend's swing before the dice land; if it hits, it bites deeper.

roster.name: Ayoka
roster.line: A chanter of oríkì, Oyo's praise poetry, who knows every lineage's glories and the parts it leaves out.
roster.scene: A festival day in Akinwale's quarter of Oyo Ile, drums everywhere. A handsome woman in an indigo wrapper chants each family as it passes, louder for the ones who tip. You are a stranger, and she greets you with a line of praise for your grandfather, made up on the spot, which is already better than anything he did. The drummers pick it up. By evening children in the next compound are chanting it.
roster.play: You know everyone's story, and a well-placed line of it can make a foe falter at the worst moment.
roster.class_note: Carries the words: song, story and memory that change a room.

signature.name: Cutting Words
signature.line: A line of praise poetry turned sharp, so a foe's blow or boast falls short.

roster.name: Bibi Oysha
roster.line: A Bukharan woman teacher who writes the talismans for her father's lodge and teaches the science of letters to girls the madrasas won't take.
roster.scene: The courtyard of a Naqshbandi lodge in Bukhara. A woman of fifty-two draws a square of letters on a doorframe in saffron ink, reciting as she writes, and a whole courtyard of girls recites it back. When she finishes, the doorframe is a door that nothing unwelcome will pass, and every girl in the courtyard knows how she did it.
roster.play: Your work is protection: a ward of letters on yourself and anyone near who needs it.
roster.class_note: The licensed scholar of magic, most likely to hold a post.

signature.name: Arcane Ward
signature.line: A ward of written letters that takes blows before she does, and tops up with every protection she casts.

roster.name: Brites Fagundes
roster.line: A halfling baker of Lisbon's Alfama with a Mutapan cold box, whose pastries the whole quarter queues for.
roster.scene: Before dawn in the Alfama, the alleys still dark, and one doorway full of warm light and the smell of bread. A small woman with flour to the elbows slides a peel into the oven and out again without looking. Two novices in grey wait on the step for the convent's order. Behind her, a battered Mutapan box in the back room hums to itself and frosts over. She hands you a heel of yesterday's loaf, which is as good as today's, and asks if you've eaten.
roster.play: You make beautiful things people want, and in a fight you paint the field so your friends see what to hit.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: A highlight or a shadow, made to look as if it was always there.

roster.name: Brother Joris Vanhove
roster.line: A Flemish Jesuit lay brother in Beijing who casts cannon, mends clocks and checks every figure before the court's noon shadow.
roster.scene: The courtyard behind the Jesuit chapel, a quarter-hour before noon. A lay brother in a dusty cassock kneels on the flagstones with a plumb line, a chalk mark and a slate covered in figures, and when the Bureau's clerk starts to speak he holds up one hand without looking round. The shadow of the gnomon crawls toward the chalk. It stops a hair short. He says something in Flemish that a lay brother shouldn't, wipes the slate, and starts again.
roster.play: You study the gunner across the ditch and take the shot that costs him most, round any cover and at any range.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Calculated Shot
signature.line: A musket ball where the curve says it will go.

roster.name: Buatu Makaya
roster.line: A Vili merchant of Loango who carries copper up to Malebo Pool and speaks the tongue of every valley on the road.
roster.scene: The Tio market at Malebo Pool, the dry season, noon. A line of porters sets down copper bars and bales of raffia cloth, and a wiry man in good cloth bargains in Teke with one hand and keeps a tally in Portuguese with the other. Something no one quite looks at is carrying the heaviest bale, and has a great many hands to do it with. When the Tio factor names his price, the trader answers in the dialect of the factor's grandmother's village, and the factor laughs and halves it.
roster.play: On the road you are the guide who speaks every tongue; in a fight your hundred-handed spirit catches blows meant for your friends.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Favors
signature.line: The mountain's gifts: a vista opened, a ward on a friend, a spirit called.

roster.name: Chea Sok
roster.line: A Khmer former monk called by spirit illness at Angkor, who guides pilgrims through the world-mountain by night.
roster.scene: The gallery of the Thousand Buddhas at Angkor Wat, near midnight, a clay lamp on the floor. A sixty-year-old man in plain cloth points up through the gallery's opening at the central tower and describes, with complete calm, the five peaks above it, the one in the middle going up farther than the sky. Nobody else can see them. A pilgrim beside him is weeping, because she almost can.
roster.play: You guide the way and speak every tongue; your hundred-handed spirit catches blows meant for your friends.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Favors
signature.line: The mountain's gifts: a vista opened, a ward on a friend, a spirit called.

roster.name: Chuqui Ocllo
roster.line: A brewer of Cusco who keeps the valley's debts of work, and knows who owes a day to whom.
roster.scene: A courtyard in Cusco in the afternoon, a great jar of aqha working in the shade. A broad woman with her sleeves tied back stirs it with a paddle and keeps track, out loud, of who owes whom a day's work, back three harvests, while the runners' widows on the bench correct her and are wrong. A Spanish muleteer, a prisoner, sits among them with a cup. Nobody is angry. Nobody is hungry. She hands you a cup and asks what your family can do.
roster.play: You know what every household owes and is owed, and you call in the debt when it matters.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Everyone Has a Price
signature.line: An offer, made in the moment, that a hired hand has to think hard about refusing.

roster.name: Daeng Calla
roster.line: A halfling smuggler of Makassar who runs Mutapan curiosities past the Dutch on the monsoon.
roster.scene: The Dutch boarding officer has the manifest in one hand and a lantern in the other, and the lantern is the only light in the hold, because she switched off the other one with her heel when she heard him on the ladder. He asks what is in the long crate. Rattan, she tells him, and smiles, and the crate behind her, which is full of lamps that light themselves, is very quiet.
roster.play: You talk your way past customs, hide behind the officer himself, and when it comes to blades you strike where it hurts and vanish.
roster.class_note: Gets in where the doors are locked.

signature.name: Sneak Attack
signature.line: One strike a turn where it hurts most, from the shadows or beside a friend.

roster.name: Daeng Nai
roster.line: A Makassarese gunner who learned artifice third-hand and keeps the walls of Somba Opu against the Dutch.
roster.scene: Night on the walls of Somba Opu. A woman in a dark baju sets a squat brass device on the parapet with a click, checks its level twice, and walks back along the wall to where her rice is going cold. Out in the dark a Dutch working party starts digging again. The thing on the parapet turns its head, and fires, and fires, and she eats.
roster.play: You set down your turret and fire through it, from round the corner of the bastion, while you stay behind the parapet.
roster.class_note: Mutapa's artificer, whose devices are built to a standard and work.

signature.name: Turret
signature.line: A small gun set down beside her that fires when she does.

roster.name: Dom Garcia Nsaku
roster.line: A Soyo shield-bearer who carries the count's letters to people who'd rather not get them, and comes back.
roster.scene: The royal army comes down to the edge of the sacred wood in its best order, and the shield-bearers of Soyo come out to meet it dancing: the sangamento, swords flashing, shields turning, a display of every cut they mean to make. Then the dance stops, and it turns out they meant every one.
roster.play: You fight light, with a door-sized hide shield and a broadsword, and your tricks make up for the armor you don't wear.
roster.class_note: The trained professional, in the century that made war a trade.

signature.name: Superiority Dice
signature.line: A disarm, a parry, a riposte: the drilled tricks of a professional, fed by his dice.

roster.name: Domenego Cargnelutti
roster.line: A caul-born benandante of Friuli who goes out in spirit on the Ember Days to fight witches with a stalk of fennel.
roster.scene: A field outside a Friulian village on the night of the Ember Thursday, and the man fighting in it is asleep in his bed a mile away. Out in the furrows his spirit stands with a stalk of fennel in his fist and a company of the dead at his back, and across the field the witches come on with their sorghum stalks. The harvest is what they are fighting over. In the morning he wakes, eats his bread, and walks to Udine to explain all this to the Holy Office again, with a round of cheese for the notary.
roster.play: You fight beside the spirit of the great tree: a plane-strike and a fennel stalk, and a thread of fate for a friend's save.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Favors
signature.line: The Wells answering: a thread of fate, or the spirit of the tree called to his side.

roster.name: Domingas da Costa
roster.line: A food-seller of Salvador who keeps the chest of the Rosary brotherhood.
roster.scene: Sunday after Mass on the steps of the Rosary church in Salvador's lower city. A small woman in a white turban sits with the brotherhood's book open on her knees and counts the week's coins aloud, twice, so everyone can follow. A man with an iron collar scar sits beside her and watches the total. When it's done she looks up, smiles, and offers you a cake from her tray. "Buy two," she says. "One is for him."
roster.play: You feed people, keep the brotherhood's money safe and heal whoever falls; your healing counts double.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Preserve Life
signature.line: A breath of the divine that gets the fallen back on their feet.

roster.name: Dona Catarina de Sá
roster.line: An Afro-Portuguese heiress who lost her family's land when Mutapa kept its mines, and now runs Sofala's platinum runners.
roster.scene: A cook-shop by the Sofala fish market at the hottest hour, the awning flapping. A comfortable woman of forty is shelling prawns into a bowl and asks how your mother's knee is. You have never met her. Your mother's knee is bad. Across the market a tollkeeper's man is searching a porter's basket, and finds only fish, and the porter honestly cannot tell him anything else.
roster.play: You never plan out loud: when trouble comes, the boat was already waiting and the guard already paid.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The door was already unlocked, the guard already paid: a preparation she made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Dona Leonor Mvemba
roster.line: A Kongo noblewoman widowed at Mbwila, who means to bring the king's crown and scepter home from Lisbon.
roster.scene: A borrowed house in Mbanza Soyo, swept and bare. A straight-backed woman in her late husband's best cloak receives you as if the kingdom were still whole, his cross of the Order of Christ on her breast. On the table: a Portuguese grammar, open, and a list of every ship bound for Lisbon this year. She asks whether any of you can pass for Portuguese. Then she asks whether any of you can pass for a thief.
roster.play: You stand at the front and everyone near you stands steadier; your sword blazes when you call on your oath.
roster.class_note: Keeps an oath so hard it becomes a power.

signature.name: Sacred Weapon
signature.line: Her blade blazes with holy light and finds its mark more often.

roster.name: Doña Isabel Cuauhtzin
roster.line: A Nahua cacica of Xochimilco who paints miniatures for the viceroy's court, and so holds everyone's likeness.
roster.scene: A window in the viceregal palace, the light coming in sideways off the Zócalo. A marquis sits for his miniature and talks the whole time, mostly about the Audiencia, and keeps glancing at the vellum oval in her palm to see whether she's got his sleeve right. She hasn't started on the sleeve. She has his mouth exactly, the way it goes when he lies about land, and she'll paint it a hair wrong before she gives it to him. The true one she keeps.
roster.play: You paint the field: light up the foe your friends are fighting, hide the friend in trouble, and fool the eye with a painted wall.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: A highlight, a shadow or a painted door, made to look as if it was always there.

roster.name: Elena Grimani
roster.line: A Venetian doctor at Candia who links her squad into one pulse and keeps every man in it alive.
roster.scene: Candia, the twenty-first year of the siege. The Venetian doctor on the Sabbionera bastion has a wand in one hand and a tourniquet in the other, and the four men on the parapet in front of her are tied to her and to each other by something nobody else can see. When the Ottoman mine goes up under the wall, the first man down is on his feet again before the dust settles, and the second is already getting up. She steps through the air to the third before the janissary on the breach can reach her.
roster.play: You link your friends into a chain before the shooting starts, then heal anyone on it from where you stand.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Vital Stream
signature.line: One pulse, felt in every throat on the chain: her healing reaches anyone linked.

roster.name: Fadzai Shoko
roster.line: A Mutapan Vitalist who treats a whole valley as one patient.
roster.scene: The fever house on the slope above Hoerikwaggo, with the mountain behind it and the bay below. At noon she throws every shutter open and lets the day in: the wind off the mountain, the smell of fynbos, sunbirds in the aloes. She walks the beds with her sleeves rolled up, Dutch sailors and Khoekhoe herders on the same ward, and the men say afterward that it felt like being outdoors for the first time in a month. Outside the window a protea is blooming in the wrong month.
roster.play: You heal freely, and what a friend can't hold goes on to the next; when a blow lands, the ground takes some of it.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Continuity
signature.line: Healing that spills from one friend to the next, and comes back to her.

roster.name: Farrokh of Isfahan
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: An elf of Isfahan who ate at a pari wedding and made terms with the Hidden Realm itself.
roster.scene: A coffeehouse off the Maidan in Isfahan, after the evening prayer. In the corner an elf in a wedding robe gone gray at the hems lets the water pipe bubble and does not inhale; he is listening. The smoke over him takes the shape of a garden that isn't on any map of the city, then a door in the garden, then, for a moment, a woman's hand on the door. The naqqal at the front stops in the middle of Rostam. Nobody else in the room sees the hand, and the elf is already gone.
roster.play: You weave illusions from pipe smoke and step behind the world when trouble comes, taking a friend with you.
roster.class_note: Made a deal, and the other side keeps it.

signature.name: Step into the Hidden
signature.line: He steps out of the world and back in, thirty feet away and unseen.

roster.name: Ferhad Usta
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: The second master of the Topkapı confectionery, with a pari grandmother.
roster.scene: The back door of the palace confectionery at the evening prayer, steam and the smell of roses. A slender elf in a white jacket hands a cup of violet sherbet, cold as a mountain, to a porter who held the door for him that morning. Then he turns and looks at you for a long moment, the way he looks at a syrup to see whether it has set, and hands you one too.
roster.play: You make sweets fit for the sultan and see what's really in a face; in a fight you fool the eye.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: A highlight, a shadow or a painted door, made to look as if it was always there.

roster.name: Fra Bertrand de Montclar
roster.line: A gold-dragonborn Knight of Malta holding the breach at Candia in the siege's last year.
roster.scene: The mine goes up under the Sant'Andrea bastion at dawn and the breach is full of janissaries before the dust is down. He is in it with the Order's banner behind him, his sword lit like a church window, and the men on either side of him are not afraid, because standing near him they can't be. They hold the breach until noon. In the afternoon the Venetians ask him to hold another one.
roster.play: You stand where the line has to hold, and everyone near you stands steadier; when the breach fills, your breath goes across it as fire.
roster.class_note: Keeps an oath so hard it becomes a power.

signature.name: Sacred Weapon
signature.line: His longsword blazes with holy light and finds its mark more often.

roster.name: Fusipala
roster.line: A woman of a chiefly house at Lapaha on Tongatapu who keeps the order of the ʻinasi, the first-fruits gathering: whose yams, mats and kava go where, and what it means when a chief sends less.
roster.scene: The green at Lapaha in the weeks before the ʻinasi. A woman of forty-eight sits on a fine mat at the edge of it with a knotted cord in her lap, reading a canoe's tribute as it comes ashore: yams, mats, kava, and one bale fewer than last year. A young chief strides up to explain. She tells him, gently, which of his uncles he has just insulted, and how to make it right before dark.
roster.play: You keep a great household in order, and when trouble comes the help you need was already arranged.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The canoe was already waiting, the gift already sent: a preparation she made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Ganonhsese
roster.line: An Onondaga Clan Mother who chooses her clan's chief for the Grand Council, and wants to know why the drumming started with no drummer.
roster.scene: A longhouse at Onondaga in midwinter, snow on the roof, the fires down the middle. An older woman shells beans with her daughters while a council chief stands before her and explains himself. She doesn't look up. When he is finished she says three sentences, and he sits down. Outside, faint and steady, a drum is beating in the woods where no one is drumming.
roster.play: You speak and the council listens; you bargain with what lives past the edge of things for your people.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Strike a Bargain
signature.line: A bargain struck through her god, and its people do the work.

roster.name: Garabed Vanetsi
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: An Armenian porter of the Istanbul quays with a push in him nobody can see.
roster.scene: The bronze culverin is coming off the cart wrong, and six hamals are under it when the rope parts. It stops. It hangs a yard above them with nothing holding it, and on the quay their kâhya, who hasn't moved, says in Armenian, "Out, then," and when they are out he lets it down onto the cradle as gently as a basket of eggs. The Venetian spy on the next pier writes very fast.
roster.play: Your power builds every turn; you brace inside your own push, and your release shoves a foe off the quay.
roster.class_note: Has a raw force coming through them that builds until it's let out.

signature.name: Release
signature.line: Force let out on one foe, pushing it straight back.

roster.name: Gaukhar
roster.line: A Kazakh aqyn unbeaten in the sung contests for six years.
roster.scene: A feast on the autumn pasture, a dozen yurts, the whole valley come to watch. A young woman with a dombra across her knee answers a challenger's verse before he has finished it, rhyming on his own last word and turning it on him. His uncle laughs first. Then everyone does. The challenger, scarlet, laughs too, and asks for another round. She plays the first notes before he has finished asking.
roster.play: You out-sing anyone, and you fight the same way: a quick line, a quick blade, never out of breath.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: The poet's gift for making the hard thing look effortless.

roster.name: Gelong Tsereng
roster.line: A Khalkha Buddhist monk of Erdene Zuu who heals the sick on the herding round.
roster.scene: The courtyard of Erdene Zuu, a brazier burning. A monk of forty-five sets a felt ongon on the coals, with real regret, and watches it burn. Then he turns to the woman who made it, takes her hand, which she burned trying to snatch it back, and bandages it, gently, saying a prayer for her.
roster.play: You ride from camp to camp and heal whoever is ill; your healing counts double.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Preserve Life
signature.line: A breath of the divine that gets the fallen back on their feet.

roster.name: Gennaro Esposito
roster.line: The majordomo of a Neapolitan crime family, who keeps its house fed, seated and talking.
roster.scene: A back room above a chandler's shop: one lamp, three ledgers, a Mutapan lamp in a crate marked as candles, and a boss who wants to know why the shipment was late. The majordomo doesn't answer that. He tells him which customs clerk was bought by whom, which of their own runners was taken last night and what that runner knows (nothing that matters; he saw to it), and that the other family will make an offer on Thursday, which the boss should refuse, and then accept on Saturday. Then he closes the ledger. It's not personal.
roster.play: You never plan out loud: you get into trouble, then reveal that the guard was already paid and the boat already waiting.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The door was already unlocked, the guard already paid: a preparation he made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Golnar
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A pari of Isfahan who ties knots between people and things, and speaks the terms aloud.
roster.scene: The Maidan at Isfahan at dusk, the fountains lit and the polo goalposts throwing long shadows. A young woman in green that nobody else seems to notice sits down at the party's table, and every water flask they carry is suddenly full of rosewater. She ties a knot in a green thread between the merchant across the table and the fountain behind him. “You will stay,” she says, very kindly, “until you have told me where the cup is.” He finds that he will.
roster.play: You tie a knot and a word in one breath: stay, spare, or come here, and they find they must.
roster.class_note: Fae-touched, folding space and season, with a piece of the Hidden inside.

signature.name: Warps
signature.line: Knots of the Hidden, tying one creature to another place or person.

roster.name: Gottlieb von Schleich
roster.line: An envoy to the Perpetual Diet at Regensburg, who travels everywhere and knows what every court will do next.
roster.scene: A reception in Regensburg, candles, the Diet's envoys in their second-best coats. At the edge of a conversation that matters stands a damp, attentive Freiherr of about fifty with a glass he never drinks, and he laughs a moment after everyone else. He remembers your mother's name and your debts. He offers you, unasked, a small piece of help, and it is exactly the help you needed. Later you see him writing in a small green book.
roster.play: You have someone inside every closed room, and you know what each of them wants before they say it.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Network
signature.line: Someone already inside any closed place in the city, who owes him a favor.

roster.name: Gu Wenyuan
roster.line: A gold-dragonborn calendar clerk of Beijing's Astronomical Bureau, who has found a Ming prince's sealing date that doesn't add up.
roster.scene: A teahouse below the observatory on Beijing's city wall, past midnight. A clerk of the Astronomical Bureau does long division on the back of a tea bill, his sleeve pulled down over the golden scales on his wrist. He finishes, checks it, and goes pale. A Ming prince's tomb was sealed on a date the sky could not have allowed. Either the Bureau's records are wrong, or the tomb isn't what it says.
roster.play: You read the sky and the record, and in a fight you call out the path that gets your friends clear.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Course Correction
signature.line: "Left! Now!": a called path that lets his friends move clear.

roster.name: Hafız Ömer
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A young preacher of Istanbul, honest, learned and certain that the lodges and the coffee are innovations.
roster.scene: Friday, a neighborhood mosque in Istanbul. A young preacher with a voice that fills the dome preaches against coffee, and fifty men nod. On the steps afterward a porter is groaning over a foot crushed under a cask; the preacher kneels, prays, and the bone sets under his hands. "Baraka!" the crowd says. The preacher stands up, visibly annoyed. "It is God," he says, "not me, and not the saint at the lodge," and walks off to carry an old dervish's shopping home for him.
roster.play: You preach and the light answers you: it burns the dark away and turns aside the blows aimed at your friends.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Radiance of the Dawn
signature.line: A flash of holy light that burns away magical darkness and sears the foes around him.

roster.name: Hakim Ishak Toledano
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A Sephardic physician of Edirne's old hospital, who reads the nerves and sends his medicine along them.
roster.scene: The domed hall of Bayezid's hospital at Edirne, where the water runs in a fountain under the dome and five musicians play for the patients three times a week. An old man in a physician's robe holds a patient's wrist and counts against a sand-glass. Without looking up, he says that the drummer is late. The drummer, who is not late, plays faster. The patient's pulse comes down to meet it.
roster.play: You heal from across the room and steady a friend's mind when it's about to break.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Reflex
signature.line: Healing sent along the nerves to a friend thirty feet away.

roster.name: Hinewai
roster.line: The kaikaranga of a Waikato hapū, the woman whose call opens the way for visitors onto the marae.
roster.scene: The gate of a marae on the Waikato, a visiting party halted outside it. On the far side an older woman in a feather cloak lifts her voice: a long, high call that names the visitors' ancestors and her own, and weeps for the dead of both, all in one breath. A woman among the visitors answers. The two calls cross the open ground. You find, to your surprise, that you are weeping too. Then the gate is open, and everyone is going in to eat.
roster.play: Your voice opens and closes the way; it steadies your people and unsettles whoever comes against them.
roster.class_note: Carries the words: song, story and memory that change a room.

signature.name: Cutting Words
signature.line: A call that unsettles a foe so its blow or boast falls short.

roster.name: Hoʻolulu
roster.line: A kahuna lāʻau lapaʻau of Kona, a healer by plants and prayer, who treats everyone the same whoever holds Kona.
roster.scene: A fisherman's house in Kona, fever in the air. A man of fifty-seven kneels by the sleeping mat with a gourd of pounded leaves. Before the medicine touches the fisherman's lips he pauses and says the plant's name, and its prayer, all of it, and does not hurry for the fisherman's wife, or for the chief's man waiting at the door. Then the fever breaks.
roster.play: Your healing comes out of someone else: you rip life from a foe and give it to a friend.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Rip Life
signature.line: Life torn from a foe and handed to a friend.

roster.name: Hu Lanxin
roster.line: A fox spirit in a woman's shape on China's tomb road, who remembers what she is and changes luck with a palmed card.
roster.scene: A sealed Ming tomb, the night the party finally breaks through. The lamp finds a woman in a scholar's daughter's silk sitting on the prince's coffin, eating the party's dried plums out of the party's bag. “What took you so long?” she says. When the tomb's guardian brings its blade down on the tomb robber, she turns over a leaf card, and the blade finds the stone floor instead.
roster.play: You palm a lot and change someone's roll after it lands; when it goes wrong, you are a fox and gone.
roster.class_note: Fae-touched, folding space and season, with a piece of the Hidden inside.

signature.name: Warps
signature.line: Lots readied in the palm and springs set in the ground, ready to turn luck fair or foul.

roster.name: Hywel Bowen
roster.line: A Welsh parson who goes between his village and the Hidden: bread held out, iron put away, no names.
roster.scene: The church bell has been going since sunset, and the man ringing it is nearly sixty and out of breath. Between peals he leans out of the tower and calls down into the mist in Welsh, politely, the way you'd speak to a neighbor who has your cow: a child went missing at the ford, and he would like to talk about what would be fair.
roster.play: You talk first, and a fight you never have is the one you win; if talk fails, you heal and turn the riders aside.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Channel Divinity
signature.line: The go-between's gift, which turns the Hunt aside at the flood and brings the fallen back at the ebb.

roster.name: Iliqa
roster.line: An Evenki shaman of the upper Lena, chosen by a dead shaman's spirit, who walks the Tree's three worlds for her clan.
roster.scene: A dark tent at the winter camp on the upper Lena. A woman of forty drums until the rim of the drum frosts over, her coat's iron pendants ringing. When she stops, she tells the elders exactly where the sable went this year, and how many the forest can spare, and that it will not be enough for the fort.
roster.play: You fight beside the spirit of the great tree, and swap places with it to put yourself where you're needed.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Favors
signature.line: The Wells answering: a thread of fate, or the tree's spirit called to her side.

roster.name: Ilyanor Sael
roster.line: The elf who heads Lanternhall's Long Ward at Basel, and already knows the answer.
roster.scene: Rounds on the Long Ward at the sixth bell. A tall elf in a coat of pale azure stops at the foot of bed twelve and reads the patient from there: the fever, the pulse in her throat, the one thing in her that is failing. He doesn't touch her. "Diagnose her," he tells the student beside him. "Then tell me what you'd do. Then don't do it yet." Inside the coat his hand rests on the rod, and stays there.
roster.play: You diagnose at a glance and heal from your own life's store; at the table you are the one who knows, and says so.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Healing Prowess
signature.line: A touch with a little of the Font in it, and a wound closes.

roster.name: Iya Adunni
roster.line: Mother of the palace market at Oyo Ile, who hears everything that is said over a stall.
roster.scene: Midday where the cloth row crosses the pepper row in the palace market at Oyo Ile. A heavy woman on a low stool eats bean cakes and listens to two traders shout about a length of cloth. When they run out of breath, she names which of them is right, which of them owes which esusu circle this week, and what the cloth is really worth, in one sentence. Both of them pay her the fee. Beside her a Mutapan lamp on a pole hums in the sun.
roster.play: You know what every face is hiding, and in a fight you shout the warning a heartbeat early.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Forewarned
signature.line: A shouted warning that lets her friends brace for what the enemy is about to do.

roster.name: Johanka Vlková
roster.line: A Prague geomancer in Rudolf's overgrown garden, who draws the Hidden's geometry without the Hidden.
roster.scene: In the Royal Garden at dusk she paces out a square in the long grass that nobody else can see, drops to her knees at its corner, and draws four rows of dots in the dust with her finger. The Jesuit with her asks, as they all do, whether she is some fortune teller. "Tonight they come over the Stag Moat," she says, "from the north, about an hour after moonrise. Stand where I put you."
roster.play: You draw a figure on the ground and it does exactly what it says: knocks a rider sideways, or holds a creature in a circle.
roster.class_note: The licensed scholar of magic, most likely to hold a post.

signature.name: Figures
signature.line: A fixed shape drawn on any surface she can see, affecting only whom she chooses.

roster.name: Josiah Thorne
roster.line: A Boston coroner who views every sudden death and keeps finding that the bewitched died of something with a name.
roster.scene: A lane off the Boston waterfront, early, frost on the cobbles. The dead man lies where he fell, and the magistrate standing over him is quoting Exodus. The coroner kneels without answering, holds a brass rule to the dead man's eye, then turns his hand over and looks at the nails for a long time. He writes down the magistrate's verse, and the width of the pupil, on the same page, and asks the jury of neighbors which of them sold the man his bread.
roster.play: Most of your work is before and after: you read the room and the body; in the fight, you find the flaw that makes your foe easier to hit.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Find the Flaw
signature.line: The join in anything, found: its guard drops for as long as he studies it.

roster.name: Juana de la Luz Quispe
roster.line: A beata of Lima, a chandler's daughter by a Quechua mother, whose light comes from inside her and whom the Holy Office watches.
roster.scene: The notary of the Holy Office brings her the letter at dusk, as he always does, and stands with his back to her, as he always does, so he can say afterward that he didn't see. She takes off her veil. The gold comes up in her eyes, and the scraped-away lines come up out of the paper underneath the ones a forger wrote over them, and she reads him the name that was there first. It is his superior's.
roster.play: Your power builds every turn; what you light can't hide, and your friends see it clearly.
roster.class_note: Has a raw force coming through them that builds until it's let out.

signature.name: Release
signature.line: Light let out on one foe, so it can't hide and the next blow finds it.

roster.name: Kaiawa
roster.line: A Waikato tohunga of Aotearoa who has seen the far side of the ocean the dead sail for, and come back.
roster.scene: A pā above the Waikato in the gray before dawn, the mist down on the ridges. Somewhere up in it a flute is playing, and a young woman of the pā has got up from her mat and is walking toward the palisade with her eyes open and nobody behind them. A woman with red ochre on her hands steps into her path and opens her palm, and water rises out of the packed earth between them, clear and cold, with a pale light over it like the moon on a pool. The girl stops. She looks at the water, and then at the tohunga, and then she is crying, and herself again, and the flute on the ridge goes quiet.
roster.play: You open a spring under your friends that heals whoever is hurt, and call the blessed dead to stand beside them.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Wellspring
signature.line: The River of Life rising in a spring underfoot, healing the hurt who stand in it.

roster.name: Kalehua
roster.line: A chief's daughter of Kona, three times surfing champion at the Makahiki games.
roster.scene: Dawn on a beach at Kona, the swell coming in long and glassy. A tall young woman with a board taller than she is sits on the sand, reading the waves and refusing to say whether today's the day. Two chiefs' sons are waiting for her answer. She stands, runs, and is out past the break before either of them has his board. When she comes in on the biggest wave of the morning, she is already chanting a verse about how slow they were.
roster.play: You fight like you surf: all in, raging, with the sea's strength in you.
roster.class_note: Fights in a fury that is a state of mind, and is hard to put down.

signature.name: Rage
signature.line: She rages: blows glance off her, hers land harder, and the wild comes into her.

roster.name: Kathrin Fehrenbach
roster.line: A Black Forest woodcarver, taken into the forest as a child and given back with the Names of things.
roster.scene: A farmhouse above Furtwangen, the window open to the forest. A woman at a carving bench hands you a wooden spoon before you've told her your name, and your name is cut into the handle. Up the valley something the size of a hill turns over in its sleep, and she stops carving and listens until it is still. On the bench, under a cloth, lies a stave she has never finished.
roster.play: You name a creature and then call it, by name, into a loop or a hill you made for it.
roster.class_note: Fae-touched, folding space and season, with a piece of the Hidden inside.

signature.name: Warps
signature.line: Staves cut with a creature's Name, and the places she can call it into.

roster.name: Kawennanoron
roster.line: A Mohawk Wolf Clan matron at the Eastern Door of the Haudenosaunee.
roster.scene: The first hearth inside a Mohawk longhouse at the Eastern Door, smoke going up through the roof hole. An older woman ladles corn soup into a bowl for a Dutch trader, a different bowl for a Mahican runner, and a third, smaller and plainer, for a French priest. A girl beside her watches which bowl goes to whom. "Why that one?" the girl asks in Mohawk. "Because he will ask for more," her grandmother says, "and I want him to."
roster.play: You keep the household and its counsel; your word decides more than most warriors' arms.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The message was already sent, the canoe already waiting: a preparation she made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Kenzhe
roster.line: A Kazakh rider taken by the pari three winters ago, who came back riding ahead of the Wild Hunt.
roster.scene: Just past the camp's watch fires, the dark half of the year. A rider sits his horse at the edge of the light, smiling his old smile, and calls the watch by their childhood names: the boy who was afraid of the dark, the girl who stole his apricots. One of the watch takes a step toward him before his sister's hand catches his collar.
roster.play: You shoot first and take second: the one who falls is gone into the Hidden until someone calls its name.
roster.class_note: Knows the ground, and what comes over it.

signature.name: Take
signature.line: The prey vanishes into the Hidden until someone calls its name.

roster.name: Kesavan Vaidyan
roster.line: A Kerala surgeon whose family craft is the rebuilt nose, and whose knife goes where he sends it.
roster.scene: A veranda in a Malabar compound in the monsoon light. A soldier from the war of noses sits very still, drugged and steady. The surgeon has cut a leaf to the shape of a nose and laid it on the man's forehead; now the knife hangs in the air beside the soldier's face, held by nothing, and draws the line around the leaf as slowly as a man writing his name. The surgeon's hands are folded in his lap. He is watching the patient's breathing, not the knife.
roster.play: You work from a distance: the floating knife cuts your foe, and the healing goes with the cut to a friend nearby.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: The Incision
signature.line: A cut from the floating scalpel at a foe up to sixty feet away.

roster.name: Khadijeh Khatun
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: The stewardess of the shah's mother's household, called the Key, who decides which letters and rumors go in.
roster.scene: A garden pavilion in the royal harem at Isfahan, the fountain loud, a carved screen between you and the woman who asked for you. The sherbet is already poured: one cup for each of you, though nobody told the gate how many were coming. Through the screen a pleasant voice tells you three things about yourselves that you did not know anyone in Persia could know, and asks for nothing at all. Yet.
roster.play: You know who answers to whom, what they fear and what they'd sell, and somewhere in every house is someone who owes you.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Network
signature.line: Someone already inside any closed place in the city, who owes her a favor.

roster.name: Khodadad the Dyer
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A Zoroastrian dyer of Isfahan who was set on the throne to take the bad stars off the shah, and still has them.
roster.scene: A dye yard in Isfahan's Zoroastrian quarter, vats of indigo and madder steaming. A heavy, cheerful man stands knee-deep in a blue vat, arms blue to the elbow, and waves at you, hoping you're a customer. When you tell him who sent you, he sits down in the dye. A pigeon lands on the rim of the vat, looks at him, and falls in.
roster.play: You carry the shah's bad luck and somehow keep winning; you call your friends' swings before the dice land.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: The Count
signature.line: He calls a friend's swing before the dice land; if it hits, it bites deeper.

roster.name: Kichibei
roster.line: A tempura seller at the foot of Nihonbashi in Edo, whose hot oil is the start of his experiments.
roster.scene: Dusk at the foot of Nihonbashi, a stall of planks and a pot of oil hissing. A wiry man with a towel around his head lowers river fish in a pale batter, lifts them out gold, and hands them on skewers to a porter and a samurai standing side by side, which they would never do anywhere else. Between batches he scribbles in a notebook: the oil's heat, the batter's weight, the weather. He glances across the bridge, where another stall is selling fish that can't be in season, and his mouth goes thin.
roster.play: You carry two experiments a day and choose their energy as you throw; sometimes they bite back.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Experiments
signature.line: Two sealed vessels a day, each released in the energy he chooses as he mixes it.

roster.name: Kilimoar
roster.line: A keeper of Nan Madol on Pohnpei who asks the world for its shape, and gets it.
roster.scene: He has been sitting cross-legged on the platform since the rain started, eyes shut, one hand flat on a fallen column as long as a canoe. The Mutapan with the notebook has been waiting three hours. Then the old man laughs, pats the stone twice, and says, "All right." The column rolls over once, like a sleeper, and lifts, and walks itself up onto the course where it was always meant to lie, and the Mutapan drops his pencil in the sea.
roster.play: You shape the land with every turn: a rampart against the muskets, a pillar for a friend, roots that hold the brute in place.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Shape the Land
signature.line: Basalt and coral rise where he asks: a rampart, a pillar or a grasping root.

roster.name: Kima Ismare
roster.line: A Wounaan jaibaná of the Chocó, hired by her people to keep a river shut against the mining families.
roster.scene: A stilt house on the upper San Juan, where the miners' canoes stop and turn back. Under the house a woman of fifty-five sits cross-legged with carved wooden staffs laid out before her, talking to something in the river that isn't the river. A canoe comes round the bend, full of men from Popayán. The current changes. The canoe goes back the way it came, and its paddlers can't say why.
roster.play: You keep a river shut by bargain and by will; whoever wants it open has to get past you.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Strike a Bargain
signature.line: A bargain struck with the spirits through her god, and its people do the work.

roster.name: Kit Harrow
roster.line: A gambler in breeches at the Restoration court, married (she says) to a poet who says otherwise.
roster.scene: The card room at Tunbridge Wells in August, the windows open on the walks. A woman of twenty-four in breeches and a man's waistcoat keeps the bank at basset, and two earls and a bishop owe her more than they've told their wives. She has never once been seen to count. Across the room a young man recites something about country squires, and she raises the stakes without looking at him.
roster.play: You read the room and every mark in it, call your partner's thrust before he makes it, and walk away with the pot.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: The Count
signature.line: She calls her partner's thrust before he makes it; if it lands, it bites deeper.

roster.name: Kunhi Ayesha
roster.line: A Mappila pepper broker on the Calicut beach who sells the Zamorin's officers news of every ship, and the ships news of them.
roster.scene: The pepper weighing on the Calicut beach, under a palm-leaf awning. A woman of forty sorts peppercorns between finger and thumb without looking at them, and repeats, word for word, what a Dutch captain said three tables away a minute ago. Nobody on the beach has ever seen her write anything down.
roster.play: You know what everyone wants and whom they answer to, and you sell it to the person who needs it most.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Forewarned
signature.line: A shouted warning that lets her friends brace for what the enemy is about to do.

roster.name: Kunwar Ratan Singh
roster.line: A younger prince of a minor Hada Rajput house, serving in the Mughal army of the Deccan, who fences like water.
roster.scene: The practice ground of the viceroy's camp at Aurangabad, first light. A drunk officer swings at a young Rajput prince over a debt, and the prince takes a single step inside the swing, stops the sword with two fingers on the man's wrist, and apologizes for the inconvenience. The officer sits down in the dust. The prince helps him up, and asks after his horse.
roster.play: You challenge the biggest thing in the room and stand between it and whoever it came for.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: Effortless arms: the riposte, the step in front of a friend.

roster.name: Kusi Wallpa
roster.line: The Sapa Inca's senior staff officer on the Apurímac front, who reads Spanish columns by their dust.
roster.scene: A cold rock above the road a Spanish column must take, the Apurímac far below. A man of fifty-two sits with a khipu across his knees, tying knots without looking at the cord, eyes on a smudge of dust on the far ridge. A runner shifts from foot to foot behind him. "Two hundred," he says, "forty horse, six guns, and they have not eaten since yesterday." He ties one more knot. "Empty the storehouse at Limatambo by tonight."
roster.play: You know the enemy's numbers before they arrive, and in the fight you call every move a step ahead.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Exploit
signature.line: He calls the weak point, and whoever strikes it strikes harder.

roster.name: Lala Sukhdev
roster.line: A Multani moneylender in Bukhara's caravanserais, lending to herders, khans and students at rates set by how far they live from Multan.
roster.scene: An upper room in the Indian caravanserai at Bukhara, carpets, ledgers and a pot of tea. A plump man in a white turban counts a herder's loan onto a cloth, coin by coin, twice, so the herder can follow, and writes the sum in a ledger the herder can't read and trusts anyway. He looks up at you, smiles, and asks how far you live from Multan, because that is how he sets his rate.
roster.play: You know what everyone owes, and the crew you hire is paid on the spot.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Everyone Has a Price
signature.line: An offer a hired blade has to think hard about refusing.

roster.name: Lihpahnu
roster.line: Sehpin's elder sister on Pohnpei, who grows the family's prize yams for the chiefs' feasts and calls that the real work.
roster.scene: Red earth above the lagoon, a terraced yam garden. A broad woman with mud to the elbows straightens up, wipes her face with the back of her wrist, and looks you over. "You're here for my sister," she says. "Everyone is. Sit. Eat first." Behind her a yam vine as thick as your arm climbs a pole twice your height.
roster.play: You grow things and feed people, and the land you tend lends you its strength when it's needed.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Land's Aid
signature.line: The land's own strength, hurting foes and healing a friend in one breath.

roster.name: Lisabetta Mannucci
roster.line: An instrument-maker's daughter of Florence who writes to the Royal Society under her brother's name.
roster.scene: Her father's workshop near Santa Croce. A young woman in a leather apron sets a sealed flask on a balance, adjusts the rider to a grain, writes the figure down, and turns to the visiting priest. "Bless it, please," she says. "Anything you like. Then I'll weigh it again." He hesitates. She has already dipped her pen.
roster.play: You carry two experiments a day and pick the energy as you throw: lightning, thunder, acid, frost; sometimes it bites you back.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Experiments
signature.line: Two sealed vessels a day, each released in the energy she chooses as she mixes it.

roster.name: Lu Qingxu
roster.line: A fallen court alchemist of the Qing hills who knows how the old imperial tombs work.
roster.scene: Under the hill, the tomb's last door is sealed with a talisman older than the dynasty that buried the prince. He reads it by lamplight, twice, and writes his own beneath it in cinnabar. The door opens. Behind it, something that has been waiting since the Ming sat up when the paper went on, and he raises the lamp to see whether it's the elixir or the reason no one came back.
roster.play: You scout every door before anyone opens it, and this morning's omens let you set a roll before it's made.
roster.class_note: The licensed scholar of magic, most likely to hold a post.

signature.name: Portent
signature.line: Two dice read this morning, set in place of any roll he sees.

roster.name: Mai Raji
roster.line: The cook of the free kitchen at the Sikh gathering in Dhaka, who feeds everyone who comes.
roster.scene: Dusk in the courtyard of the sangat in Dhaka, an iron griddle the size of a cartwheel over the fire. A broad woman in a white headscarf slaps out flatbread with her bare hands, faster than anyone can eat it, while a Mughal trooper, two Bengali boatmen, a Portuguese deserter and an Armenian merchant sit in one line on the mat. She hands the trooper a bowl and points him, without a word, at the pots. He goes and washes them.
roster.play: You feed everyone and protect everyone; when your oath calls, your ladle's as good as a sword.
roster.class_note: Keeps an oath so hard it becomes a power.

signature.name: Lay on Hands
signature.line: A healing touch from a pool she spends as she needs.

roster.name: Manekbai Parekh
roster.line: A Jain shroff's widow who runs her late husband's banking house in Surat, and writes notes honored from Mocha to Malacca.
roster.scene: A cool upper room near the customs house at Surat, the weeks before the ships sail. A widow in white does sums aloud in Gujarati, faster than the English president's writer can do them on paper, and corrects his figure kindly. Then she turns to you, names the rate at which she will stake your voyage, and you can see her deciding, as she says it, how much she likes you.
roster.play: You know what everything is worth and who is paying for it, and you buy the fight off before it starts.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Everyone Has a Price
signature.line: An offer a hired blade has to think hard about refusing.

roster.name: Matthias Kessler
roster.line: An apothecary's assistant nobody looks at twice, who knows exactly what is in every cup.
roster.scene: A banquet hall after the guests have run. The host is face down in the sauce, and his taster sits beside him, untouched, wiping his gloves. A serving girl in the doorway draws breath to scream. The taster looks up, raises one finger to his lips, and says nothing at all. She doesn't scream. Later she will tell the magistrate she can't describe his face, and she will be telling the truth.
roster.play: You win before the fight: you read every glove and body, and when it comes to blades, you wait for the one hit that finishes it.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Poison
signature.line: A dose on the blade that leaves its mark poisoned.

roster.name: Mirza Bahram Sabzevari
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A Persian courtier who moves a reception one guest at a time, and keeps everyone's head.
roster.scene: The columned porch of the Chehel Sotoun at an evening reception, the twenty wooden pillars doubled in the long pool. A young mirza recites a ghazal of his own at the shah's table, lays down the cup on the last line, takes up a bow in the garden, and puts an arrow through a pomegranate at forty paces. He doesn't watch it split. He's already asking the Georgian envoy about the roads to Tiflis, and the envoy, charmed, is telling him.
roster.play: You change minds in conversation without anyone noticing, keep your friends steady, and heal the one who falls.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: Composure for everyone near him, and the conversation that brings a guest round.

roster.name: Mirza Qasem Beg
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A giant-blooded master of the Isfahan practice ground, who taught half the young officers at court.
roster.scene: The practice ground of the royal ghulams by the Maidan, an hour after dawn. A Qizilbash captain who has insulted a Georgian has been told the terms: one blade each, the circle chalked on the sand, first blood ends it, and nobody touches the fallen man's horse. The captain is still settling his grip when the giant across the circle takes one step along a chord. A line of red opens on the captain's sleeve. The giant bows, wipes the khmali, and asks a boy to read him the note that came from the palace, because he has never been able to make sense of the hand.
roster.play: You challenge the biggest thing in the room and stand between it and whoever it came for.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: Effortless arms: the riposte, the step in front of a friend, the cut that makes it look easy.

roster.name: Morfudd Prys
roster.line: A Welsh dwarf who keeps her village's gate against the Wild Hunt with iron and salt.
roster.scene: The bell in her hand is the size of a sexton's, and she rings it once at the gate. The mist on the lane doesn't move, and then it does: a white hound, red-eared, that was a patch of fog a moment ago, and behind it riders with no faces she can hold in her eye. The iron nails in the gateposts are warm. She nocks an arrow and says the name she has been saving.
roster.play: You read the tide each evening and ward the gate before the Hunt comes; your iron arrows find what glamour hides.
roster.class_note: Knows the ground, and what comes over it.

signature.name: Cold Iron
signature.line: Iron in every arrow: a harder hit, and a Hidden creature can't teleport away.

roster.name: Munyaradzi Shava
roster.line: Master of the merchant house that carries the king's shewstones abroad, who weighs people the way his clerks weigh gold.
