roster.scene: The counting room of the Shava house in Sofala's new quarter, the scales polished, the clerks silent. Its master is beautifully dressed and perfectly courteous, and he has not blinked since you sat down. You make your offer. He repeats it back to you, word for word, including the part you tried to say quickly, and asks whether that is the weight you meant it to have.
roster.play: You never raise your voice; you remember every word said, and you wait for the moment it matters.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Poison
signature.line: A dose on the blade that leaves its mark poisoned.

roster.name: Mustafa Remzi Efendi
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: The Ottoman court's chief astrologer, who picks the sultan's hours and knows it is mathematics.
roster.scene: The Topkapı, an hour before dawn. The court is waiting in the cold for the sultan to ride out, and the sultan is waiting for one man. On a terrace above the Bosphorus an old astronomer in a sable-lined kaftan holds a brass astrolabe at arm's length, then a water-clock, then the astrolabe again. He does arithmetic on a slate. He lifts one finger. Down in the court, a hundred men breathe in, and the drums begin.
roster.play: You study a foe and turn the room's own laws on it, and you call out the path that gets your friends clear.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Course Correction
signature.line: "Left! Now!": a called path that lets his friends move clear.

roster.name: Mwalimu Bakari Shee
roster.line: A Bajuni pilot of Pate island who knows which waters take a toll, because what lives under them once took him.
roster.scene: The deck of a Gujarati ship off the Lamu archipelago, the monsoon steady astern. The pilot drops a sounding line, hauls it in, and looks at what is on the tallow for a long moment: not sand, not shell. "Not here," he says, to nobody the captain can see, and drops a twist of cloth with something in it over the side. The captain laughs. The pilot has stopped trying to warn captains who laugh.
roster.play: You know the safe channel and the haunted one, and when it goes wrong you step behind the world.
roster.class_note: Made a deal, and the other side keeps it.

signature.name: Step into the Hidden
signature.line: He steps out of the world and back in, thirty feet away and unseen.

roster.name: Nafisa al-Qalyubiyya
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A Cairo plague doctor who knows the quarantine law of every port she enters.
roster.scene: A plague lane at Bulaq, below Cairo, where the carts have stopped coming. A woman in a dark wrap and veil walks into a house with a censer on a rod and a ledger under her arm. A gold haze settles out of the censer over the household on their mats, and over the next hour the fevers break, one by one, and she writes each name down. Two men looting the empty house next door come out with their arms full and walk into a gray haze instead. By evening they are coughing, and the man who went in to help them is too.
roster.play: You heal a whole room with one golden cloud, and know where a sickness came from and where it will go.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Miasma
signature.line: A cloud of restorative vapor that heals one friend and steadies all of them.

roster.name: Nane Gulbahar
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A Tabriz midwife who keeps the forty days after a birth against the Āl, and has never lost a mother to her.
roster.scene: A courtyard in Tabriz, past midnight, the new mother asleep behind the door. An old woman on a stool across the doorway cracks pistachios, an iron sickle on her knees. Something thin, with a nose of clay, looks round the courtyard gate. Nane doesn't get up. She says its name, the real one, quite conversationally, and it goes. Then she goes back to the pistachios, and a few minutes later, to sleep.
roster.play: You ward the door before the danger comes, and your iron finds what hides from everyone else.
roster.class_note: Knows the ground, and what comes over it.

signature.name: Cold Iron
signature.line: Iron in every blow: a harder hit, and a Hidden creature can't teleport away.

roster.name: Ndona Mvita
roster.line: A palm-wine seller of Mbanza Soyo whose bench is neutral ground.
roster.scene: Sundown under the great tree in the plaza at Mbanza Soyo. A woman with a gourd pours palm wine for a Capuchin, a nganga, a Dutch factor and two of the count's shield-bearers, all on one bench. The factor says something about the count. The shield-bearers stiffen. She tops up the factor's cup, says one word in Kikongo, and the bench laughs, the shield-bearers loudest. Nobody remembers afterward what the word was.
roster.play: Everyone talks at your bench and you hear all of it; in a fight you talk the whole time and slip every blow.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: The gift for making the hard thing look effortless.

roster.name: Ndona Nsimba
roster.line: A nganga of Soyo who heals, divines, guards against the ndoki and seals the count's treaties.
roster.scene: The edge of the sacred wood of Nfinda Ngula at dusk. A broad, laughing woman with white chalk on her brow binds an oath bundle in cloth and cord, an nkisi under her other arm like a market basket, while a Dutch trader waits with a fever in his face. She names her price for the cure. He argues. She laughs, and puts the price up.
roster.play: You heal and divine, and the land lends you its strength when you need it.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Land's Aid
signature.line: The land's own strength, hurting foes and healing a friend in one breath.

roster.name: Ned Ashcombe
roster.line: A Restoration poet with a good leg, a better ear and a lampoon in his pocket that will get him killed.
roster.scene: The Groom Porter's, Whitehall, past midnight. A young man in a good coat with a frayed cuff leans on the back of a chair at the hazard table and recites a couplet about the king's spaniels. Half the room laughs. The woman in breeches at the table doesn't look up; she doubles her stake, because the couplet rhymed on "king," and the king means the bank is weak.
roster.play: You talk the whole fight: put on a mask from the comedy, fence with a rapier and an insult, and turn the blow that should have hit you.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: The courtier's gift for making the hard thing look effortless: a riposte, a mask, a hair not out of place.

roster.name: Neeltje Claesdochter
roster.line: Leiden's licensed ice-reader, who says which ice will bear.
roster.scene: Dawn on the Rhine at Leiden, the ice still grey. A small, broad woman in three skirts walks ahead of the first skaters, tapping with a pole, drilling a hole with an auger, muttering over a knot of red wool. Behind her the town waits on the bank. She stops, listens, and points: that way bears, that way doesn't. By noon she is frying pancakes at her stall and refusing hot zopie to a student who skated the wrong way anyway.
roster.play: You read the ice and the weather and say which will hold; the land lends you its strength when it doesn't.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Land's Aid
signature.line: The land's own strength, hurting foes and healing a friend in one breath.

roster.name: Nurbibi
roster.line: A gnome of the Central Asian steppe who writes up its little monsters as animals, and would rather take them alive.
roster.scene: A blind of felt on a ridge of red sandstone, the ninth day. Below, on a shelf of quartz still warm from the sun, a beast the size of a sheep with a beak and a bony frill is settling over a clutch of eggs. Her grandmother called it a griffin, an eagle-headed lion that guarded the khans' gold. It is not. It is a mother, and the quartz holds the day's heat into the night. She writes that down, in a careful hand, and the date, and then she draws its foot.
roster.play: You learn before you shoot: what it fears, what it eats, how it fights; then the musket, or the stonebow to bring it down alive.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Calculated Shot
signature.line: A shot placed where her study says it will tell.

roster.name: Nyarai Soko
roster.line: The master of the Mhizha Guild, who turned the great artificer's discoveries into a craft anyone can learn.
roster.scene: Entry day in the guild hall. A heavy-set woman in a chemist's leather apron stands at the lectern with a vial from every batch of the week lined up beside her, reading each new journeyman's name aloud twice. A Portuguese factor in the gallery asks, loudly, how anyone knows the vials are any good. She picks one at random, unstops it, drinks it, and reads the next name.
roster.play: You win the fight in the morning: elixirs made and handed out before anyone draws, then the gun, or medicine with your Bonus Action.
roster.class_note: Mutapa's artificer, whose devices are built to a standard and work.

signature.name: Tria Prima
signature.line: Elixirs made at the morning's bench: Salt that heals, Sulfur and Mercury that sharpen.

roster.name: Ok Rye-hwa
roster.line: A Korean mudang outside Seoul's walls who bargains with the spirits for her neighbors.
roster.scene: A gut outside Seoul's walls, the drums going since dusk. A woman of forty-seven in a general's hat dances barefoot on the blades of two fodder-choppers, and laughs at the faces of the scholars watching from the back. One of them sent for her. He will not say so in daylight.
roster.play: You talk to the spirits first, and a fight you never have is the one you win; when talk fails, you heal.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Strike a Bargain
signature.line: A bargain struck with the Hidden through her god, and its people do the work.

roster.name: Olaniyi
roster.line: Master of the Alaafin's horse, who knows to the animal how many mounts Oyo has and how many the forest will kill.
roster.scene: The royal stables at Oyo Ile, a week before the dry-season campaign. A heavy, quick-eyed man stands in the dust with a tally-stick in each hand and a groom at each elbow, and the horses are led past him one by one. He looks at your horse before he looks at you. Then he tells you how old it is, where it was bought, what it ate this morning, and that it will be dead before the rains if you take it south of the forest's edge.
roster.play: You see the whole field before anyone moves, and tell your friends where to strike.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Exploit
signature.line: He calls the weak point, and whoever strikes it strikes harder.

roster.name: Osaretin
roster.line: A master of the oba's guild of brass-casters at Benin, who casts the court's history in metal.
roster.scene: The casters' street in Benin City in the heat of a pour, the furnace roaring. You may watch from the doorway, and not one step further. A thickset man with burn scars to the elbows lifts the crucible himself. Afterward he wipes his hands, looks at where each of you is standing, and tells you who among you is in charge, who thinks they are, and who is going to argue about it later. Then he asks how they draw a plaque in Amsterdam, and with what.
roster.play: You cast history in brass and read faces like metal; in a fight you light up the foe your friends are fighting.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: A highlight or a shadow, made to look as if it was always there.

roster.name: Panay
roster.line: The eldest sister and head of an Amis house on Formosa's east coast.
roster.scene: Dusk on a house platform above the east coast, the mountains black behind it. A tall woman with betel-red teeth pours millet wine for a Chengtian trader, two Atayal visitors and a sunburned Japanese castaway, all on one mat. She is teaching the castaway his first Amis word, which is the word for more. Below in the field her youngest daughter is pretending not to listen to a young man singing.
roster.play: You run a great house and read the land it lives on; the land lends you its strength when your people need it.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Land's Aid
signature.line: The land's own strength, hurting foes and healing a friend in one breath.

roster.name: Perundevi
roster.line: Keeper of a pilgrim rest house on the Alagar road outside Madurai.
roster.scene: Before dawn at a chatram on the Alagar road, forty pots on forty fires. A woman of sixty with a ladle in each hand stirs two at once and asks every pilgrim who comes in where they walked from. When you tell her, she names the next village on your road, the well that's gone bad and the temple cook who will feed you there. Then she hands you rice, and remembers your answer for the rest of her life.
roster.play: You feed and house whoever comes, and when trouble walks in you already know who it is.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The bed was already made, the gate already shut: a preparation she made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Piero Neri
roster.line: A Florentine wool-carder and captain of the Misericordia, the brotherhood that carries the sick and buries the dead.
roster.scene: The bell rings on the cathedral square at two in the morning. Six men in black robes and hoods come out of the brotherhood's house with a stretcher and set off at a trot. You can't see their faces. One of them, broad-shouldered, smelling faintly of raw wool, stops long enough to kneel by you in the street, put his hand on the cut on your arm and close it, and say, "Thanks be to God. Go home." Then he is gone after the others.
roster.play: You go where the sick are, carry them out and heal them; your healing counts double.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Preserve Life
signature.line: A breath of the divine that gets the fallen back on their feet.

roster.name: Ponni
roster.line: A potter-priest's daughter near Madurai who helps make Ayyanar's terracotta horses, and has started riding out behind them.
roster.scene: The Ayyanar shrine outside a village near Madurai on a dark night, a hundred clay horses pale in the starlight. A girl of seventeen walks the boundary with a sickle and a clay lamp, talking to the horses as if they were her brothers. One of them answers. She doesn't stop walking. Behind her, very quietly, something big and invisible keeps pace, its hooves making no sound on the dust.
roster.play: You ride the village boundary at night; your iron finds what the glamour hides.
roster.class_note: Knows the ground, and what comes over it.

signature.name: Cold Iron
signature.line: Iron in every blow: a harder hit, and a Hidden creature can't teleport away.

roster.name: Rakhmabai Deshmukh
roster.line: A Maratha widow who took the fort's keys from her husband's belt and has held it for Shivaji since.
roster.scene: The gate bastion of a hill fort in the Western Ghats, at dusk, the wind coming up the scarp. A woman in a widow's white sari, the end of it over her head against the wind, reads the plain below with a Dutch glass. "Forty horse, no guns, and they've eaten," she tells the havildar beside her, before he can see the dust at all. "A patrol, not a column. They'll camp at the second well. Light the lamps on the north wall, so they count them." He goes to light the lamps. She goes back to counting the Mughal fires, and to the letter she is writing to the man across the plain about their next game of chess.
roster.play: You win the fight before it starts, then spend it calling targets and directing your allies' blows.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Exploit
signature.line: She calls the weak point, and whoever strikes it strikes harder.

roster.name: Ramji Parekh
roster.line: A Gujarati struck from the guild's rolls, who teaches anyone in Sofala who can pay and draws charts that fold the ground.
roster.scene: A rented godown behind the Sofala quay, after dark. A plump, cheerful man in white cotton has a map spread on a crate, and the map is drawing the room as the captain walks in: the crate, the lamp, the captain's own feet. "Your lamps will be ready by the morning tide," he says. "No stamp. And this," tapping the margin, where a line of ink is still crawling, "is the rock off Bazaruto your pilot doesn't know about. That part is extra."
roster.play: You draw the ground steeper than it is, knock a crowd down, and fold a cornered friend out of trouble.
roster.class_note: Mutapa's artificer, whose devices are built to a standard and work.

signature.name: Folds
signature.line: Space folded: a slope drawn under a crowd, or a friend moved from one place to another.

roster.name: Rashid bin Khamis al-Ghafiri
roster.line: An Omani captain with the storm in his blood, raiding the Portuguese down the Swahili coast.
roster.scene: Off Mombasa, with Fort Jesus's guns run out and the Portuguese galleon closing, the wind drops dead and every man on the dhow looks aft at the captain. His hair is standing up. The compass on the binnacle is pointing at him. He says, in a voice they hear from the bow, "Hold on to something," and the sky over the galleon goes white.
roster.play: Your power builds every turn like weather; you call lightning on the enemy deck and let it all out on the one who matters.
roster.class_note: Has a raw force coming through them that builds until it's let out.

signature.name: Release
signature.line: The storm built up inside him, let out on one foe and forking to more.

roster.name: Saadat Ali
roster.line: An Agra bridegroom who went to a pari wedding for one night, came back after three years and found himself married twice.
roster.scene: A lane near the Jamuna in Agra at midnight. A young man in a slightly too splendid coat sits on the doorstep of his bride's family's house, plucking a rabab, a tune he never learned. Every dog in the lane has come to lie down and listen. Upstairs, a shutter opens an inch, and closes again. He keeps playing.
roster.play: You charm, you dodge, and when it all goes wrong you step behind the world and are gone.
roster.class_note: Made a deal, and the other side keeps it.

signature.name: Step into the Hidden
signature.line: He steps out of the world and back in, thirty feet away and unseen.

roster.name: Saliha Hatun
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A widow of Üsküdar whose charitable endowment dresses poor brides.
roster.scene: A bench by a marble fountain in Üsküdar, its water cold even in August. An old woman in a fine plain cloak goes through a wedding dress with a young man in a trustee's turban, pricing the lace aloud, and the young man winces at each figure. She turns to you and asks, quite pleasantly, whether you know anything about ledgers. The young man winces harder.
roster.play: You know what everything costs and who is paying, and you spend it where it does the most good.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Everyone Has a Price
signature.line: An offer, made in the moment, that a hired hand has to think hard about refusing.

roster.name: Salvu Zammit
roster.line: A Maltese chirurgeon of the old school, saw in hand, who stands in the door of the ward.
roster.scene: The great ward of the Sacra Infermeria at the evening meal, every patient eating off silver. A galley in from Candia has sent up its wounded, and the first through the door is a knight carried by four oarsmen, one leg wrong below the knee. The chirurgeon looks at the wound, then at the boots, and asks which galley. He is already rolling his sleeves over the breastplate. "Count the dishes back in," he tells the orderly, "all of them," and takes the saw down from its hook.
roster.play: You stand in front with a saw and heal yourself with every hit; the enemy has to come through you to reach the wounded.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Under the Knife
signature.line: A hit with the saw that mends him as it cuts.

roster.name: Sardaana
roster.line: A Sakha singer who leads the round dance at the midsummer festival on the Lena meadows.
roster.scene: Midsummer on the meadow above the Lena, and the sun won't set. A young woman in a beaded headdress with a horsehair whisk in one hand has pulled a Cossack's Sakha wife, a Russian clerk and you into the circle by the elbow, and is singing a verse about each of you. The circle answers. She makes a verse about the clerk's boots. The whole meadow laughs, and the clerk, to his own surprise, keeps dancing.
roster.play: You lead the dance and the songs, and the land lends you its strength when your people need it.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Land's Aid
signature.line: The land's own strength, hurting foes and healing a friend in one breath.

roster.name: Sarongelug
roster.line: A palu of Polowat, a master navigator of the Carolinian wayfinding schools, who holds the star compass in his head.
roster.scene: A voyaging canoe a day out from Polowat, no land in sight. An old navigator lies in the bottom of the hull with his eyes shut, reading the swells through his back. "Pikelot," he says, naming an island over the horizon, and adjusts nothing, because the canoe is already pointed at it. The Dutch passenger checks his chart, finds the island, and stops checking his chart.
roster.play: You never get lost, by sea or land, and in a fight you see which way the blow will go before it lands.
roster.class_note: Uses the laws the world already obeys, with no magic at all.

signature.name: Course Correction
signature.line: "Left! Now!": a called path that lets his friends move clear.

roster.name: Sehpin
roster.line: A priest of Pohnpei who can still ask the basalt to move, and keeps the people inside the walls alive.
roster.scene: A Spanish pilot off the reef sees it from the deck: a column of black basalt, longer than his ship's mast, lifting out of the shallows and laying itself crosswise on a wall that was already old. The figure standing on the wall doesn't look up at the ship. When the pilot asks his crew what they saw, none of them will say.
roster.play: You heal, and your healing counts twice; out of a fight you raise and mend stone that no crew could lift.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Preserve Life
signature.line: A breath of the divine that gets the fallen back on their feet.

roster.name: Ser Marin Zorzi
roster.line: One of Venice's three State Inquisitors, a tiefling who has walked the last bridge and weighs everyone he meets.
roster.scene: A windowless room with gilded stars painted on its ceiling, a long table, and no clerk taking notes. The accused stands; the judges sit; one of them wears a plain white mask and says nothing at all. When the accused lies, the small brass figure at that judge's elbow turns its head. When the accused calls on whatever he called on to get him out of the last court, the masked judge looks up, and the man finds he can't speak, and the room goes cold, and somewhere very far off a bridge creaks under a weight.
roster.play: In court the fight is words and seals; in a fight you weigh the accused and take the blow meant for the one beside you.
roster.class_note: Has seen the real shape of the worlds beyond, and opens small gates to it.

signature.name: Favors
signature.line: The planes answering: a vista opened on the Bridgehead, and the accused Weighed.

roster.name: Shen Xuanji
roster.line: A fallen court alchemist in Beijing, compounding mineral elixirs for rich men and racing Lu Qingxu to the Ming tombs.
roster.scene: The back room of a medicine shop near the Drum Tower, after dark, by introduction only. It smells of mercury. A handsome man who looks forty-five pours a red elixir into a jade cup, and it glows faintly in the lamplight. The glow is the only part of it he made with magic. The rich man across the table drinks it, and feels ten years younger, for an hour.
roster.play: You make people see what isn't there, and your illusions are harder to see through than anyone's.
roster.class_note: The licensed scholar of magic, most likely to hold a post.

signature.name: Improved Illusions
signature.line: Illusions cast without a word, and reaching farther than they should.

roster.name: Shi Yuanjing
roster.line: A Shaolin fighting monk waiting to see what the new dynasty wants with armed monasteries.
roster.scene: The bannermen came up the valley road to count the monks, and the abbot sent him down to meet them alone, with a staff and nothing else. The officer asked what the staff was for. He set its foot on the road, walked three steps up the face of the gate tower as if it were the road, and sat down on the lintel to wait for the next question.
roster.play: You spend your focus every fight: a flurry of staff and fists, a strike that stuns, a step that runs up the wall.
roster.class_note: A body trained until it's a discipline, and the discipline works.

signature.name: Focus
signature.line: Focus spent on a flurry of blows, a step of the wind or a patient defense.

roster.name: Shiri
roster.line: Mutapa's spymaster, who runs its foreign service from one room above the House of the Bird.
roster.scene: One room above the House of the Bird in Sofala, its shutters half closed against the noon. A plain woman of fifty sits at a plain table with a dozen letters laid out in front of her like a hand of cards, and a cup of tea that went cold an hour ago. You came up the stairs to give her your name. She gives it to you first, then the name of the ship you came in on, then the name you used on the ship.
roster.play: You are never in the room where the fighting is; you knew it was coming, and you told the right people first.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Forewarned
signature.line: A shouted warning that lets her friends brace for what the enemy is about to do.

roster.name: Shushan Ghukasian
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: The widowed head of a New Julfa silk house, whose credit is good from Amsterdam to Manila.
roster.scene: A counting room off the Vank cathedral square in New Julfa, bales of raw silk to the ceiling and a clerk copying a bill of exchange into Armenian, Portuguese and Dutch. The widow at the desk reads the bill, then the manifest, then your faces, in that order. Before you have said why you came she offers you a contract for the monsoon, Bandar Abbas to Surat, paid in credit good from Amsterdam to Manila. Then she tells you why you really came: her son.
roster.play: You pay for results on the spot, and the crew you hire fights harder for knowing it.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Everyone Has a Price
signature.line: An offer, made in the moment, that a hired blade has to think hard about refusing.

roster.name: Simbarashe Moyo
roster.line: The grandfather of Mutapan artifice: the man who showed lightning is electricity, old now and wary of Europe.
roster.scene: The merchant house's men come to the workshop at night to take back what the court says is the court's. The old man doesn't get up. He lifts the old arc gun off the bench, the one that started as a lightning rod, and the construct in the doorway stops being furniture. The first man through gets the strike, and the second gets what it jumps to.
roster.play: You fire the arc gun every turn and your iron construct strikes beside you; out of a fight there is nothing you can't name, open or fix.
roster.class_note: Mutapa's artificer, whose devices are built to a standard and work.

signature.name: Construct
signature.line: An iron companion that moves at his word and strikes when he fires.

roster.name: Simon Horowitz
roster.line: A Kabbalist given a book by the archangel Michael, whose angels answer as he deciphers it.
roster.scene: Past midnight, at a borrowed table at the back of a study house, a candle-end and a book in a script nobody living reads. Simon Horowitz has the eleventh page open and the twelfth almost. The candle leans toward the page, and the room is suddenly much too bright, and something tall stands behind his chair, reading over his shoulder, waiting to see if he gets the next word right.
roster.play: Each fight you call an angel and send it on one errand: to mend, to guard or to strike.
roster.class_note: Made a deal, and the other side keeps it.

signature.name: Call an Angel
signature.line: An angel lands beside the fight, does one errand, and leaves; once in each fight.

roster.name: Sir Jasper Kellaway
roster.line: An English knight with a license, a gauge on his chest and a clerk who writes down where he sleeps.
roster.scene: The bravo's blade is an inch from Ned's throat when the lanterns along the fondamenta all lean toward the masked Englishman at once. He says, "Oh, damn," in the tone of a man who has spilled wine on a host's carpet, and the bravo's cloak catches, and keeps catching, and the bravo goes into the canal on his own, which everyone agrees was the sensible thing to do.
roster.play: Your power builds every turn; you wreathe yourself in fire and let it out on one foe, where it catches and burns.
roster.class_note: Has a raw force coming through them that builds until it's let out.

signature.name: Release
signature.line: Fire let out on one foe, where it catches like dry thatch.

roster.name: Sister Ondine
roster.line: The senior night sister on Lanternhall's Long Ward, who can't cast a spell and is the one person every Physician obeys.
roster.scene: Three in the morning on the Long Ward, one lamp lit. A small, square woman in a grey habit moves down the beds with a cup of water, and stops at one where a patient has asked for it in a certain way. She sits down beside him and stays. On her way back she finds a Physician asleep on his feet against a pillar, takes his elbow, steers him to an empty bed and puts a blanket over him, and he lets her.
roster.play: You run the ward: everything you need is already where you left it, and the doctors do what you tell them.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: About That
signature.line: The bandage was already laid out, the door already locked: a preparation she made earlier, revealed now.

roster.name: Sossi
roster.line: A market woman of Allada who has come to the beach at Offra to buy her brother back before the company ship sails.
roster.scene: The beach at Offra beside a company lodge, a ship riding at anchor beyond the surf. A woman in her best indigo cloth kneels on a mat and counts cowries into strings of forty, and strings into heads, and never once looks at the ship. A factor's clerk watches her from the lodge door. When she finishes she stands, ties the last string, and asks you, very calmly, whether you can talk to a captain.
roster.play: You know what everything is worth, and you will pay what it takes, or talk the price down to what you have.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Everyone Has a Price
signature.line: An offer a hired hand has to think hard about refusing.

roster.name: Stanisław Gołyński
roster.line: A Polish noble riding to the royal election with frost on his breath in July.
roster.scene: Three men are waiting for him at the inn: a Frenchman with a pension, a Swede with a license, and a Mutapan factor with a brass lamp that is warm to the touch. Stanisław sits down on the bench by the stove, which frosts over under him, and puts his hands out to the fire, which leans away. "Gentlemen," he says. "Which of you has come to buy me, and which of you has brought the lamp?"
roster.play: Your power builds every turn; you skin yourself in rime, and your release stops a foe dead in its tracks.
roster.class_note: Has a raw force coming through them that builds until it's let out.

signature.name: Release
signature.line: Frost let out on one foe, slowing it and stopping its reactions.

roster.name: Tadhg Ó Laoi
roster.line: An Irish fiddler who played one night under the hill and came home a hundred years late.
roster.scene: He comes down the boreen in the morning playing, the way he went up it, and the dog at the first farm doesn't know him. The farm isn't the farm. The woman at the door asks in Irish whose he is, and he names his father, and she crosses herself, because his father's name is on a stone in the churchyard that the lichen has nearly covered. He asks what year it is. Then he sits down on the step, and plays her the tune he learned last night, and she sits down beside him and cries for a reason she couldn't tell you.
roster.play: You play songs nobody taught you and they change the room; every borrowed tune goes on a tally the Hidden will collect.
roster.class_note: Carries the words: song, story and memory that change a room.

signature.name: Bardic Inspiration
signature.line: A bar of the fiddle that steadies a friend's hand or voice when it counts.

roster.name: Tapiwa Marufu
roster.line: An mbira player of Sofala who plays every spirit ceremony in the new quarter.
roster.scene: A courtyard in Sofala's new quarter after dark, beer out, a crowd of journeymen and their grandmothers. A lanky young man with an mbira in a gourd resonator plays a pattern that loops and loops until you can't find where it starts. Somewhere above the courtyard, one of the guild's singing birds starts to sing the other part. The grandmothers look up. A woman in the corner sits down hard, and speaks in her dead father's voice.
roster.play: You play and the room changes; your music steadies friends and throws foes off their stroke.
roster.class_note: Carries the words: song, story and memory that change a room.

signature.name: Cutting Words
signature.line: A phrase of the mbira that throws a foe off its stroke.

roster.name: Tetua
roster.line: A young ʻarioi of Raʻiātea, a traveling performer whose troupe mocks the chiefs in dance and verse.
roster.scene: A chief's performance ground in Tahiti, torches, the whole household watching. A young dancer of nineteen steps out and walks across the ground, and it is the chief's walk, exactly: the belly first, the pause to be admired, the glance to see who noticed. His own sons can't breathe for laughing. The chief laughs too, a moment late. Then he sends her a pig.
roster.play: You perform the whole fight: put on a mask, mock the mighty, and slip the blow that should have hit you.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: The performer's gift for making the hard thing look effortless.

roster.name: Teungku Fatimah
roster.line: A scholar at the court of Aceh's queen who writes the talismans on the port's walls and buys every book on the Monsoon Road.
roster.scene: The harbor wall of Aceh, lime-washed and new. A woman in a white headcloth writes a square of Arabic letters on it with a reed pen, each letter smoking faintly as it dries. A Dutch captain on the quay watches, and decides to send a polite letter instead of his boats.
roster.play: You write the talismans and throw the fire, and even a foe who ducks it still feels it.
roster.class_note: The licensed scholar of magic, most likely to hold a post.

signature.name: Potent Cantrip
signature.line: Her cantrips still bite when a foe dodges them: half the harm on a miss or a save.

roster.name: Tinashe Gumbo
roster.line: A Mutapan Mhizha who came out along the Monsoon Road to learn how Pohnpei's stones were raised.
roster.scene: The edge of a Nahnmwarki's feast house on Pohnpei, waiting for leave to see Nan Madol at night. A Mutapan in a work coat sits on a canoe hull taking notes, while an iron construct holds a sunshade over him with perfect patience. He asks every passing child the Pohnpeian word for something: hammer, wall, why. The construct, he has noticed, waits at the door before he reaches for the latch. He would like to know whether the basalt does the same.
roster.play: You fire the arc gun and your iron construct strikes beside you; out of a fight you ask everyone how things work.
roster.class_note: Mutapa's artificer, whose devices are built to a standard and work.

signature.name: Construct
signature.line: An iron companion that moves at his word and strikes when he fires.

roster.name: Tonderai Shumba
roster.line: A gate captain of Mutapa's capital in a lion-helmed powered suit, one of the king's lions.
roster.scene: The Portuguese have rushed the gate twice. The third time the lion in the gateway lets the first man reach him, takes the blow meant for the boy beside him, and the copper mane stands straight up. Then the lion speaks, at three hundred feet, and the line behind the man stops.
roster.play: You stand in the gap and nothing moves you; you take the hit meant for the one beside you, and the suit turns it into your next shot.
roster.class_note: Mutapa's artificer, whose devices are built to a standard and work.

signature.name: Kinetic Charge
signature.line: The suit drinks a blow and gives it back on his next shot.

roster.name: Tseren Dorji
roster.line: A Dzungar noble official in the Ili valley who wants his khan's brother brought home before the half-brothers move.
roster.scene: The khan's tent in the Ili valley, felt walls, a feast. A half-brother of the khan raises a cup and gives a long toast to brotherhood. Beside the door a zaisang stands with his hand never far from his saber, and while everyone else listens to the toast he counts the men by the door, and the men outside it, and the horses saddled at this hour of the night.
roster.play: You fight like a drilled professional, with a trick for every opening.
roster.class_note: The trained professional, in the century that made war a trade.

signature.name: Superiority Dice
signature.line: A disarm, a parry, a riposte: the drilled tricks of a professional, fed by his dice.

roster.name: Tsitsi
roster.line: A Khoekhoe go-between at Hoerikwaggo, the Cape, useful to four powers at once and owed by people in all of them.
roster.scene: The harbor under Table Mountain, a Dutch longboat at the quay, an English one beyond it, Mutapa's harbor master on the steps, and a cattle-trading party come down from the chiefdoms. Every one of them is waiting for the same woman. She is twenty-five, she speaks all four of their languages, and she is translating the Dutch captain's offer into Shona for the harbor master exactly, word for word, and into her own language for her uncle with one word changed.
roster.play: You read what people want, whom they answer to and what they'd sell, and somewhere nearby there's always someone who owes you.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Exploit
signature.line: She tells a friend where the opening is, and the blow lands harder.

roster.name: Waman Illa
roster.line: A storm priest of the Andes who survived a lightning strike and keeps a huaca.
roster.scene: On the ridge above the Spanish column the cloud has been building all morning. He stands in the spray of it with his sling hanging loose, and the first bolt comes down on the captain's horse because he asked it to. Then the wind takes him up, and the arquebusiers below learn why the high ground holds.
roster.play: You call the lightning and throw the sea's wrath at whoever stands on the ledge.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Wrath of the Sea
signature.line: Spray and storm around him for ten minutes, shoving the nearest foe back with cold.

roster.name: Wang Yuezhen
roster.line: A tanci singer at Suzhou's Chang Gate, who sings the long stories with a pipa.
roster.scene: Afternoon in a teahouse by the Chang Gate, every table full. A woman in a plain blue gown plays the pipa on a little stage and sings the young scholar's letter to his love, and half the room is servants who should be on errands. She reaches the line where the letter is found by the wrong person, and stops. The room groans. She smiles, sips her cold tea, and says, "Tomorrow."
roster.play: You sing the long stories, and a well-placed line of one can make a foe falter.
roster.class_note: Carries the words: song, story and memory that change a room.

signature.name: Cutting Words
signature.line: A line from a story that makes a foe's blow or boast fall short.

roster.name: Wat Ellery
roster.line: A border-born rider of the Wild Hunt who doesn't kill what he hunts: he takes it.
roster.scene: The dark half, the moon three days from full. A light in the mist on the low field that looks like a lantern in a cottage window, and a voice from behind it calling the shepherd's boy by the name only his mother uses. The boy stops to catch his breath. Beside him, a young man in a jerkin his grandfather might have worn, a flint-headed arrow on the string, not drawing it, and an oak bucket chained at his hip.
roster.play: You lead your prey onto thin ground with a lantern and a mist, shoot first, and take the one who matters.
roster.class_note: Knows the ground, and what comes over it.

signature.name: Take
signature.line: The prey vanishes into the Hidden until someone calls its name.

roster.name: Willka Mamani
roster.line: A Kallawaya healer of Charazani, walking the war's roads with a mule and a thousand plants in his head.
roster.scene: A mule track on the line between the armies, above the clouds. A Spanish muleteer lies shaking with fever against a cairn, and the old man kneeling beside him has a pinch of cinchona bark between two fingers. "This costs," he says, in a voice that means it. Two deserters come up the track to see what the mule is carrying. The old man looks at the first of them, and the blood leaves the deserter's face and goes into the muleteer's, and the muleteer sits up. The second deserter decides the mule is carrying nothing.
roster.play: Your healing comes out of someone else: you rip life from a foe, give it to a friend, and curse the one who needs cursing.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Rip Life
signature.line: Life torn from a foe and handed to a friend.

roster.name: Wäldä Mika'el
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: An Ethiopian däbtära who writes God's secret names on parchment and chants poetry of double meaning.
roster.scene: In a Gondar courtyard a child is screaming at something no one else can see. The däbtära unrolls the scroll he finished at dawn, the length of the child, the names in red, and the thing on the child's chest finds itself standing inside the lines of an eight-pointed star it can't get out of. He begins to sing.
roster.play: Your work is protection: a ward on yourself, a circle around the demon, a scroll on the client.
roster.class_note: The licensed scholar of magic, most likely to hold a post.

signature.name: Arcane Ward
signature.line: A ward of written names that takes blows before he does, and tops up with every protection he casts.

roster.name: Wälättä Śellase
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A widow of Gondar whose honey wine and whose feast-day gatherings nobody forgets.
roster.scene: The twenty-first of the month, a courtyard in Gondar. A tall widow in white pours tej from a long-necked flask for priests, masons and a däbtära who are all arguing on one bench, while a spear leans by the door with nobody to carry it. She lights a candle for Mary, and the courtyard is suddenly bright as noon, which nobody remarks on. Then she asks you, quite directly, what you are short of.
roster.play: You keep the feast and the faith, and when trouble comes, the light answers you.
roster.class_note: Carries a holiness that works, and answers for it to a church or a god.

signature.name: Radiance of the Dawn
signature.line: A flash of holy light that burns away magical darkness and sears the foes around her.

roster.name: Yusuf Rais
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A corsair captain of the Algiers taifa who knows what every man on a deck is worth, and pays it.
roster.scene: A galley's stern in the roads off Algiers, the city white on its hill behind. A Livorno merchant has come out under a flag of truce with a chest and a list of names. The captain doesn't open the chest. He reads the list, bites one coin, and names a price for each man on it in Spanish dollars, Venetian sequins, and Algerian sultanis, without looking up. Two of the names, he says, are worth more than the merchant thinks, and he would like to know why.
roster.play: You win boardings by buying the crew off the enemy's deck; what can't be bought, your own crew handles with you calling the shots.
roster.class_note: A brilliant mind without magic, right more often than anyone likes.

signature.name: Everyone Has a Price
signature.line: An offer, made across a deck, that a hired blade has to think hard about refusing.

roster.name: Zanetta Bon
roster.line: A halfling of the Venice rooftops who folds doors into walls and takes the way nobody else can.
roster.scene: Venice, Carnival, an hour before dawn. A small woman in a bauta mask and a soaked cloak runs the ridge of a roof above the Rio di San Barnaba with three of the Council of Ten's men a roof behind her. The canal is forty feet down and twenty across. She doesn't slow. She steps off the edge into nothing, falls, and comes out of a door in the side of the campanile across the water still falling sideways, lands running on the next roof, and the door closes behind her like a shutter. The men stop at the edge. One of them has dropped his lantern into the canal.
roster.play: You are the way in: you know every drain and servants' stair, and you step into a door on one roof and out of another.
roster.class_note: Fae-touched, folding space and season, with a piece of the Hidden inside.

signature.name: Warps
signature.line: Doors folded into any surface she can see, linked so she can step from one to the other.

roster.name: Zhamal-apa
roster.line: A Kazakh midwife who drives the albasty off birthing mothers, and pays for every life in her own pain.
roster.scene: A yurt at night, a woman in labor, every knot in the tent untied and a whip laid across the threshold. An old midwife goes to the door and shouts "The hero has come!" with such conviction that the hero, Aisulu, a head taller than the door, ducks in looking embarrassed. Something at the smoke-hole leaves in a hurry.
roster.play: Your healing comes out of someone else, and you curse whatever threatens the one you're saving.
roster.class_note: The scholar-healer, doing by study what the churches did by grace.

signature.name: Rip Life
signature.line: Life torn from a foe and handed to a friend.

roster.name: Zólyomi Benke
roster.line: A dwarf hermit on Hungary's border-castle line who raises stone walls out of a meadow.
roster.scene: The Hungarian border, a flooded meadow below a burned village, an hour after dawn. Raiders fire from the reeds, the Pasha's men or the border captain's, the reeds don't say, and the party is caught on open ground. A dwarf in a miner's jerkin drops to one knee, sets both palms flat on the mud, and barks a word at it. The meadow stands up. Where there was water there is a fort of stone, walls and a gate and a stair to the wall-walk, and the shot flattens against it like hail on a roof.
roster.play: You build the fight's ground: walls for cover, pillars to lift a raider out of reach, pits to drop one in.
roster.class_note: Fae-touched, folding space and season, with a piece of the Hidden inside.

signature.name: Warps
signature.line: Stones raised from nothing: a wall, a pillar, an opening.

roster.name: Étaín of the Ford
roster.line: A wood-elf rider in the Wild Hunt's front rank, whose fury lights her up like a torch.
roster.scene: Out of the thorn-hedge at the first dark of Samhain comes a rider whose body has turned in its skin: one eye sunk, one starting from her head, a light standing up from her brow like a mast. The great spear in her hands reaches the gatepost from the middle of the lane. Behind her the hounds; behind the hounds, someone running with a bucket.
roster.play: You wade in with a great spear and a rage that burns; the danger is going so deep you can't tell friend from foe.
roster.class_note: Fights in a fury that is a state of mind, and is hard to put down.

signature.name: Rage
signature.line: She rages: blows glance off her, hers land harder, and the hero-light rises around her.

roster.name: Čhaŋté Wašté Wiŋ
roster.line: An Eastern Dakota woman of Mille Lacs, of the wild rice and the prairie edge, who becomes the bison.
roster.scene: The hunters on foot have the herd moving toward the river breaks when one cow turns out of the dust and comes back through them, and they part for her. The thing that has been following the herd for three days, which isn't a wolf, finds out what she is when she reaches it.
roster.play: You take the bison's shape before the fight closes and charge; when the shape is spent you are still yourself, with moonlight in hand.
roster.class_note: Reads the land like a book and borrows its shapes and strength.

signature.name: Wild Shape
signature.line: She becomes the bison, with its hide and its charge.

roster.name: Đào Thị Lựu
roster.line: The head of a water-puppet guild in Thang Long.
roster.scene: Evening at a village pond outside Thang Long, the whole village eating on the bank. Behind a split-bamboo screen a dragon rises out of the water, spits a jet of spray, and chases a fisherman across the pond while the children scream with delight. When the show ends a woman wades out from behind the screen, soaked to the chest, and two girls follow her with poles. The elders on the bank don't look at the girls. Everyone else does.
roster.play: You make figures dance on water and fool any eye; in a fight you paint walls and doors where there are none.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: A highlight, a shadow or a painted door, made to look as if it was always there.

roster.name: Şerife Hatun
roster.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
roster.line: A judge's widow at the hospital in Edirne who sees the strongest passion in every face across a room.
roster.scene: Edirne, the hospital of Bayezid across the Tunca, the quiet hour after the noon prayer when the musicians rest. A patient who hasn't spoken in a year sits by the fountain under the dome. The woman beside him doesn't play anything. She watches his face, waits for the grief to come up to the surface, and when it does, she lets him see that she sees it. He speaks for the first time since spring.
roster.play: You let them come to you, stir the one who swung, and then talk it into doing what you want.
roster.class_note: The accomplished person every court holds up, who makes it all look easy.

signature.name: Ease
signature.line: Calm in the storm: wanting and fearing read at a glance, and a face that never shows her own.
